### A3-R007-01 (line 185, A3/REQ-007) — full pre-compaction record, migrated by librarian Job-3 compaction 2026-09-06
summary (full):
postReadComplete's queued lambda captures `this` (GarminConnect) but uses m_client as the QueuedConnection context; Qt's auto-cancel-on-destroy protects only the context object, so if GarminConnect is destroyed while an unowned/injected m_client outlives it with a post still pending, the dispatched lambda touches freed memory
resolved-by (full):
FIXED 2026-07-18 (hardening slice) — post context retargeted from `m_client` to a new owned bare `QObject m_completionContext` member of GarminConnect (GarminConnect.h:123, declared LAST → destroyed FIRST among members, before the CloudService base). Qt cancels the pending queued invoke when the member is destroyed, so the lambda either runs with `this` fully alive or is cancelled — UAF closed BY CONSTRUCTION in both builds; DES-014 preserved (bare QObject member ≠ Q_OBJECT on GarminConnect; no AUTOMOC added). TEST-025 (`completionContextCancelsPendingPostOnDestroy`) pins it (RED count=1 pre-fix → 0 after). Same caller-thread affinity as prior context (orchestrator-verified). QPointer<this> rejected (won't compile in the non-QObject stub TU).

### A3-R008-01 (line 190, A3/REQ-008 (inline, session-limit)) — full pre-compaction record, migrated by librarian Job-3 compaction 2026-09-06
summary (full):
REQ-008 incremental sync cannot resolve a garmin_user_id in production → readdir no-ops. Two confirmed producer-side gaps: (1) `GarminTokenStore::save` is NEVER called in production (only refs: its own def + an AddCloudWizard.cpp comment calling the save-wiring "deferred worker-in-CloudService"), so tokens.json is not written by the connect flow; (2) even if it were, `dump_tokens()` returns raw `str(self._garmin.dumps())` (garth OAuth blob) with NO top-level `garmin_user_id` key, so `GarminConnect::resolveGarminUserId()` (GarminConnect.cpp:168 `doc.object().value("garmin_user_id")`) returns empty. Result: readdir → empty uid → "no connected account; please sign in again" → no-op. Invisible to the 17/17-green suite because every unit test injects the ctor uid-override (m_garminUserIdOverride).
resolved-by (full):
FULLY CLOSED by the DEC-019 trigger-wiring slice (TEST-051/052): the wizard now drives `cloudService->persistConnectSuccess(uid, blob)` on BOTH the direct and post-MFA id-gated `succeeded(GarminAuthSuccess)` signals, and `GarminConnect::disconnect()` clears tokens on disconnect. Producer (Slice D) now has its production caller → live sync resolves a real uid end-to-end. Verification-Gate PASS: garmin 18/18, app links with the shared CloudService.h change, both paths persist, stale-reply guarded, sidecars preserved. Residual for A3 (accept-with-note): T-051 exercises the wizard→base-virtual→real-producer WIRING through a stub CloudService (GarminConnect can't link into the Python-free wizard harness — same constraint as A3-R007-02); GarminConnect's own override is covered separately by T-050 (persist) + T-052 (disconnect), so the production wizard→GarminConnect dispatch is proven only in pieces. Original analysis retained: NOT a REQ-008 defect: the three slices correctly CONSUME the DES-002 contract (uid persisted in tokens.json at first-connect). The PRODUCER side was explicitly deferred at REQ-004/006 (traceability: "C++-side persistence wiring (GarminTokenStore::save routing) rides the REQ-007-closure worker-in-CloudService lifecycle"). Fix = a separate slice/REQ: wire GarminTokenStore::save into the auth-success path AND persist garmin_user_id (wrap the blob as `{garmin_user_id, tokens:<blob>}` or write it alongside), matching resolveGarminUserId's read. Then an end-to-end test with a real (non-override) uid round-trip. Blocks the LIVE sync path only — the committed code is internally correct + fully unit-tested. Remaining A3-R008 probes (since-format contract, stage-vs-import record ordering, concurrent-guard wedge, non-dict-item mutant, RMW-over-corrupt) DEFERRED to a re-spawned qgdw-adversary after the session limit resets (9:20pm Australia/Hobart). **PARTIAL FIX 2026-07-19 (Slice D, DEC-018 B): PRODUCER built+green, TRIGGER unwired → still open.** Done: `GarminAuthSuccess.tokenBlob` carry-forward (GarminWorker success arm); `GarminTokenStore::persistConnectSuccess`(ordered tokens.json→active-account.json write)/`saveActiveAccount`/`loadActiveAccountUserId`/`clearAccount`; `resolveGarminUserId` REPOINTED to active-account.json; TEST-049 (producer unit) + TEST-050 (end-to-end, NO ctor override — LSN-024 proof). garmin-fast 18/18, app links. STILL OPEN: `persistConnectSuccess`/`clearAccount` have NO production caller — blocked on **DEC-019** (trigger insertion point). Builder surfaced 3 constraints: wizard deliberately defers config-dir routing (AddCloudWizard.cpp:180-185); the MFA success path bypasses `GarminCredentialsPage::onAuthFinished` (early-returns on MfaRequired≠InFlight) so a single trigger must catch BOTH direct + post-MFA `finished`; and there is NO `removeSettings`/disconnect virtual in CloudService.h — the DES-002 "removeSettings overridden to Disconnect" surface does not exist under that name (design↔code discrepancy → D-R008-01).

### A3-R008-F1 (line 192, A3/REQ-008 (full pass)) — full pre-compaction record, migrated by librarian Job-3 compaction 2026-09-06
summary (full):
readFile() records the Tier-1 dedup entry BEFORE the async base import pipeline confirms a parse. GarminConnect.cpp:374 (FIT) + :392 (TCX) call `recordImport(remoteid, staged)` (comment: "before completion") then `postReadComplete`; the async `CloudServiceAutoDownload::readComplete` (CloudService.cpp:1909) does `uncompressRide` and on failure `if (ride==NULL) return;` (CloudService.cpp:1937) — silent, no file written, nothing un-recorded. Since readdir's Tier-1 short-circuit (GarminConnect.cpp:459-461) unconditionally skips any id in imported-<uid>.json and Tier-2 (target-filename-exists, CloudService.cpp:1957) has nothing to catch (no file was written), a download that passes the shallow FIT magic-sniff but fails the FULL parse (truncated/corrupt/unsupported-variant FIT, or ANY tcx.ok since TCX has no sniff) is recorded-as-imported and PERMANENTLY, SILENTLY skipped on every future sync. Violates REQ-008/US-3 "incremental sync eventually gets everything." CONFIRMED on disk.
resolved-by (full):
User disposition (2026-07-20): accept for v1 + ticket. Rationale: read-only sync of Garmin's OWN generally-valid FIT exports; parse-fail is an edge; the proper fix (record-after-confirm via a base readComplete-success hook, or a reconcile pass — complicated because the sidecar records the transient staging name `garmin-<id>.fit`, not the final timestamp-named RideItem `.json`) is non-trivial and better scoped as its own slice. Ticketed as REQ-016 (prd.md), lessoned (LSN-025), and documented — NOT silently buried. Original analysis: DES-010 step 5e ordering flaw (record-before-confirm). Fix is non-trivial: import confirmation is async + downstream in the base CloudService machinery, and readFile returns synchronously before the outcome is known. Options: (1) reconcile pass — on sync, drop sidecar entries whose RideItem doesn't actually exist so they re-download; (2) record-after-confirm — new hook/signal from the base readComplete-success path (touches CloudService base); (3) accept-with-rationale for v1 + ticket (argue Garmin's own FIT is generally valid; document the corrupt-download edge). Lesson: LSN-025.

### A3-R012-F1 (line 197, A3/REQ-012) — full pre-compaction record, migrated by librarian Job-3 compaction 2026-09-06
summary (full):
**Disconnect does not stop a live, already-open()ed session — the user can keep downloading from an account they just disconnected.** `GarminConnect::disconnectService()` (GarminConnect.cpp:351-358) deletes the token files and clears NO in-memory state, and nothing enumerates or shuts down live GarminConnect instances. Reachable sequence (all four sites orchestrator-verified): AddCloudWizard finish-with-sync creates `CloudServiceSyncDialog` via `syncnow->open()` (AddCloudWizard.cpp:889-893) — **window**-modal, parented to mainWindow — over an `open()`ed GarminConnect holding a restored garth session; `ConfigDialog` is a PARENTLESS top-level QMainWindow (ConfigDialog.cpp:37-41), so Options→Athlete→Accounts→Delete is usable concurrently; `deleteClicked()` (AthletePages.cpp:164-169) mints a DIFFERENT instance and deletes tokens.json + active-account.json, never touching the live one; back in the still-open dialog, Download calls `store->readFile(...)` (CloudService.cpp:1400) which uses `m_client` with NO token re-check → activities download from the "disconnected" account. `CloudServiceSyncDialog` declares a ctor but NO destructor (CloudService.h:336) and never closes its store, and `MainWindow::syncCloud` (MainWindow.cpp:2561-2566) leaks its `db` outright — the worker thread + embedded-interpreter session live to process exit. Second-order: `recordImport` re-resolves the now-EMPTY uid and early-returns, so those downloads are imported but recorded in NO sidecar — dedup silently broken for that account.
resolved-by (full):
**RESOLVED 2026-08-03 by DEC-020 Option C (commit `f001c7d20`)** — `GarminConnect::accountStillConnected()` re-reads the on-disk credential on EVERY call (the same `GarminTokenStore::loadChecked` predicate `open()` gates on, deliberately with NO carve-out for the injected-client test seam or the uid override) and now gates both `readFile` and `readdir`; a permission-rejected token file counts as disconnected, matching REQ-006's forced-SSO behaviour. TEST-057 reproduces the exact exploit (a SECOND instance disconnects while the first stays live) and was RED pre-fix. Orchestrator ran its OWN mutation (`accountStillConnected` -> `return true`) and killed 4 slots, independently confirming the gate is load-bearing. **Residual accepted by DEC-020:** the check is inherently TOCTOU-racy (a disconnect landing between check and download still gets ONE activity through), and the restored garth session stays alive in the worker, so anything holding an `IGarminDownloadClient` directly rather than through `GarminConnect` is still unblocked. Both belong to the DEFERRED lifecycle REQ seeded by F10+F12 — Option C mitigates the reachable UI path, it does not bind session lifetime to the account. Original adjudication follows: Adjudicates B-R012-01 as a REAL defect, NOT a wording problem: the criterion clause "deletes the token file BEFORE clearing in-memory state" is not merely unencodable, it is UNIMPLEMENTED and observably exploitable. **Do not reword the clause away.** Rooted in DEC-019's choice to mint a fresh instance in deleteClicked() precisely to avoid touching live instances — so the fix reopens DEC-019 or raises a follow-on REQ; it is not patchable in design.md. The REQ-012 TEST slice itself is safe to commit (adversary's own assessment). Orchestrator independently confirmed AddCloudWizard.cpp:889-893, ConfigDialog.cpp:37-41 parentless, MainWindow.cpp:2561-2566 leak, CloudService.cpp:1400 readFile, and the absent dialog dtor. NOTE: the adversary's phrasing "no `store->close()` anywhere in CloudService.cpp" is loose — close() IS called at :1836/:1845/:1896, but only in the CloudServiceAutoDownload provider path, never by the sync dialog; the substantive claim stands.

### B-R017-02 (line 213, Builder/REQ-017 Slice A) — full pre-compaction record, migrated by librarian Job-3 compaction 2026-09-06
summary (full):
The LAZY latch (`ensureSessionLatched`) is the softest part of the epoch bind: an instance never `open()`ed latches at its FIRST `readdir`/`readFile`, binding to whatever epoch is current *then* rather than to a real session. Added because ~15 existing slots (T-048, T-055..059) drive readdir/readFile without open(); hard-requiring the latch would have broken them. It never RE-latches, so it cannot launder away a mid-session bump, and DEC-020's guard still applies — but any production path reaching readFile without open() binds itself and gains nothing from the epoch.

### A3-R017-F1 (line 216, A3/REQ-017) — full pre-compaction record, migrated by librarian Job-3 compaction 2026-09-06
severity (full):
**BLOCKING → FIXED 2026-08-05 (DEC-024, TEST-070/071; ASan-verified both directions)**
summary (full):
**Slice B's `WA_DeleteOnClose` turns the pre-existing leak into a crash.** `AddCloudWizard.cpp:892-900` creates a MODELESS `CloudServiceSyncDialog` with `setAttribute(Qt::WA_DeleteOnClose); open();`. `GarminConnect::readFile`/`readdir` run nested `QEventLoop`s (`blockingDownload`/`blockingList`/`blockingRestore`, GarminConnect.cpp:236-320), so GUI events ARE processed mid-call. A user closing the dialog then (X, or `cancelClicked()` at CloudService.cpp:980, which `reject()`s **unconditionally regardless of `downloading`**) destroys the dialog → `~CloudServiceSyncDialog` (CloudService.cpp:971-976) → `closeAndDeleteStore(store)` → **deletes the GarminConnect (and its `m_completionContext`) while `readFile` is still executing on it**; execution resumes after the nested loop returns and touches freed members. There is NO `closeEvent()` override. Orchestrator confirmed all four cited sites on disk. Adversary reproduced the crash under AddressSanitizer with TWO independent minimal harnesses (raw-QObject, and real QWidget+WA_DeleteOnClose+close() inside a nested QEventLoop) — `heap-use-after-free` on the read immediately after the nested loop returns. **This is exactly the hazard the build briefing warned about** ("getting this wrong turns a leak into a double-free/UAF, strictly worse than the bug we are fixing"); the builder reasoned it safe from Qt's DeferredDelete loop-level semantics and did NOT test it. **NOT a flaw in DEC-021's epoch mechanism** (which survived aggressive mutation) — it is a flaw in REQ-017(e)'s teardown, i.e. the very compensating control DEC-021 leans on. `MainWindow::syncCloud` is UNAFFECTED (stack-allocated, deliberately never sets the attribute — the attribute is even commented out at CloudService.cpp:436 for this reason).
disposition (full):
**FIXED 2026-08-05 (DEC-024 Option A, as amended).** The gate lives on `QDialog::done(int)` — the choke point `close()`/`reject()`/`accept()`/Escape all funnel through — plus an RAII `BlockingCall` depth counter around all four nested-loop call sites and a deferred replay once the count reaches 0. **DEC-024 as originally written was INSUFFICIENT and the builder proved it instead of following it:** on Qt 6.8.2 `reject()`/Escape destroy a `WA_DeleteOnClose` dialog even when `closeEvent()` ignores, because `QDialog::closeEvent` routes to `reject()`→`done()`. Orchestrator independently re-ran the decisive mutation: removing the `done()` gate reproduces the ASan `heap-use-after-free`; restore was byte-identical (md5 `0cd1dfb3…`) and 26/26 green. Suite 25/25 Garmin, 26/26 full, app links, ASan target passes.
resolved-by (full):
Superseded candidate list: (A) `closeEvent()` override + a blocking-call-in-flight flag set around each blocking* call, deferring destruction until the frame unwinds; (B) drop `WA_DeleteOnClose` and use the explicit-owner pattern `MainWindow::syncCloud` already proves safe; (C) revert to the leak for this one call site. Whatever is chosen MUST ship with an ASan-backed test — the adversary's own lesson is that Qt lifetime claims must be executed, not reasoned.

### A3-R017b-F1 (line 218, A3-recheck/REQ-017) — full pre-compaction record, migrated by librarian Job-3 compaction 2026-09-06
severity (full):
**BLOCKING (second route to the SAME use-after-free; also introduced by this changeset)**
summary (full):
**The DEC-024 gate is on the wrong LAYER.** It intercepts close-INITIATION (`closeEvent`/`done`), but Qt destroys child widgets **directly** when their parent is destroyed — no `closeEvent`, no `done`, no virtual dispatch. So `~CloudServiceSyncDialog` still runs `closeAndDeleteStore(store)` while a nested `QEventLoop` is on the stack, freeing the store mid-`readFile`. All four sites orchestrator-verified: the dialog is parented to `context->mainWindow` (CloudService.cpp:709), **`MainWindow` itself carries `setAttribute(Qt::WA_DeleteOnClose)`** (MainWindow.cpp:143), and the destructor (CloudService.cpp:981-987) has **no `blockingCallDepth` check anywhere**. Adversary proved the Qt behaviour with an isolated non-GoldenCheetah repro: with a `QDialog` whose `closeEvent()`/`done()` both refuse, `delete parent` ran ONLY the real destructor — neither override fired. **Exposure is not a lab artifact:** GarminConnect.cpp:41-43 sets 30s restore / 60s download / 60s list timeouts, so the window is up to a minute per call. Trigger: the user closes the athlete's MainWindow mid-sync — which the modeless dialog exists precisely to allow. **Pre-Slice-B there was NO destructor, so parent teardown LEAKED the store rather than freeing it — this changeset introduced this route too.** Widened scope: all ~16 CloudService subclasses run `QEventLoop`s in `open()`/`readdir()` (adversary grepped each), so this is not Garmin-specific.
disposition (full):
**FIXED 2026-08-06 (DEC-025, TEST-072/073, ASan-verified in BOTH directions by builder and orchestrator independently) — BLOCKING CLEARED**
resolved-by (full):
Root cause (A3-R017b-F4): the guard is wired to close-initiation, not to the operation that is actually unsafe — deleting the store while `blockingCallDepth > 0`. A destructor cannot be vetoed like a virtual `done()`, so the check must move INTO `~CloudServiceSyncDialog`/`closeAndDeleteStore`: when a call is in flight, decline to delete the store (deliberately leak, which is exactly the pre-REQ-017 behaviour and strictly better than a UAF) or hand it to a deferred reaper. Alternatives: reparent the dialog to `nullptr` for its lifetime, or a MainWindow event filter deferring teardown while a child reports busy.

summary (full):

resolved-by (full):
Fix shape: exempt tokens that are part of a known finding/claim identifier (`*-CLOSURE`, `A3-*`), or require the status word to be syntactically bound to the id (same clause / table cell) rather than merely nearby. Canonical source is `scripts/ledger_drift_lint.py` with `TEST-017`'s 15 cases (ORCH-004: NOT the installed copy in `.claude/hooks/`) — a fix needs a new case for this shape plus a re-run of `install_hook.py --extra-hook`. Cost of leaving it: prose in STATE must avoid quoting status words near ids, a small but real drag on the cursor's readability. Scores a `miss` against [[LSN-008]].  **[overflow col 7 — preserved verbatim; see 'ROW OVERFLOW' in this file's header]** **RECURRENCE 2026-08-11 (orchestrator, DEC-031 wave):** tripped AGAIN, same class — a WIKI TEST-registry note reading "the adversary's blockInReaddir variant must go GREEN" made the lint pair the token `GREEN` with **twenty** ids on that line (DEC-027/029/030, REQ-019, T-001, T-075..T-089). The lint was NOT routed around: the orchestrator reworded the hub line to drop the bare status token and point at traceability.md instead, and the lint went clean (exit 0). **Note the catch was HALF TRUE** — the false positive is real (a quoted token in prose is not a status assignment), but the underlying rule was also RIGHT: a "must go X" note in the hub IS per-id status, which DEC-015 says belongs in traceability.md. Recorded as recurrence rather than fixed, because the mechanism's prose-vs-assignment blindness is unchanged and will fire again.

### ORCH-007 (line 278, Orchestrator/ORCH-001 repair (2026-08-07)) — full pre-compaction record, migrated by librarian Job-3 compaction 2026-09-06
severity (full):
**BLOCKING-for-clean-build (PRE-EXISTING, CMake-only — the qmake build never had it) → FIXED 2026-08-07 (`427da745b`)**
summary (full):
**`CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF` (root `CMakeLists.txt:8`, `src/CMakeLists.txt:19`) silently diverged the CMake build's dialect from the qmake reference build.** Strict `-std=c++17` hides `__int128`, so Qt does not define `QT_SUPPORTS_INT128`; `qbluetoothuuid.h:391-393` then declares `QBluetoothUuid::toUInt128(QSysInfo::Endian)` — an overload a **stock Qt 6.8.2 never compiled** (built WITH int128, the call "falls back to `QUuid::toUint128()`" inline; `nm -D` shows only the old no-arg symbol exported). `Train/KurtInRide.cpp` therefore fails to link. qmake's `CONFIG += c++17` yields `-std=gnu++17` and never hits it.
resolved-by (full):
Set `CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS ON` in both CMakeLists, converging on the reference build. **Deliberately NOT fixed by adopting the uncommitted `src/Train/KurtInRide.cpp` workaround in the working tree**, which hand-rewrites the uuid→`addr64` conversion via `QUuid::toByteArray`/`fromHex` byte-shuffling: that treats a build-configuration defect as a code defect and changes byte-order handling (a silent behaviour risk for Bluetooth device IDs). Mechanism verified in BOTH directions on an isolated TU: `-std=c++17` leaves an undefined external `QBluetoothUuid::toUInt128`, `-std=gnu++17` resolves inline.

### O-R021-02 (line 290, Orchestrator/REQ-021 Phase-2 verification (2026-08-11)) — full pre-compaction record, migrated by librarian Job-3 compaction 2026-09-06
severity (full):
blocking — **HAZARD INTRODUCED BY THE REQ-021 FIX ITSELF — a read of an UNINITIALISED pointer. Found by the builder (NOTE 2), CONFIRMED and one-line-FIXED by the orchestrator.**
summary (full):
`Context::tab` is declared at `src/Core/Context.h:135` and assigned in exactly ONE place — `AthleteTab::AthleteTab` (`src/Gui/AthleteTab.cpp:35`). **`Context::Context` (src/Core/Context.cpp:141) nulls `ride`, `workout`, `videosync` and others but NEVER `tab`.** Until REQ-021 nothing read `tab` before the AthleteTab existed, so it did not matter. DEC-030 Part 1 makes BOTH dialog constructors read it. **The window is real:** `MainWindow::openAthleteTab` (MainWindow.cpp:2038) builds a `Context`, sets `athlete = NULL`, and **emits `openingAthlete(name, con)` with it**, while `context->tab` is only assigned later in `MainWindow::loadCompleted`. An uninitialised pointer handed to `QDialog(QWidget*)` is undefined behaviour — strictly worse than the UAF being fixed. **Orchestrator verified the ctor, the single assignment site, and both `new Context` sites (MainWindow.cpp:162 and :2038).**
disposition (full):
**FIXED 2026-08-11 by the orchestrator** — one line, `tab = NULL;` in `Context::Context`, with a comment naming DEC-030 and the ordering. Verified by execution: full ctest **26/26**, `GoldenCheetah` links. This eliminates the undefined behaviour; it does NOT decide the fallback policy (see the RESIDUAL).
resolved-by (full):
**RESIDUAL, deliberately NOT decided by the orchestrator and routed to A3:** with `tab == NULL` a dialog constructed on a tab-less Context becomes an UNPARENTED top-level — no crash, but nothing destroys it, so it is a leak/outlives-everything shape rather than the pre-REQ-021 `mainWindow` parenting. The alternative (`context->tab ? context->tab : context->mainWindow`) restores exactly the old behaviour, which the Part-2 rider already guards at `start()`. **Reachability of a dialog on a tab-less Context is the open question** — the builder called the `AthleteCard::configAthlete → AddCloudWizard → CloudServiceSyncDialog` route "deeply unlikely"; that is a judgement, not a proof. Adversary should settle both.

disposition (full):
**OPEN — NOT routed around.** The offending STATE.md text was LEFT AS WRITTEN, because it is correct: naming the decided mechanism in the live cursor is what STATE is for. Second false positive this session — the first (a "must go GREEN" note in the WIKI registry) WAS reworded, because there the rule was substantively right (status did not belong in the hub); here it is plainly wrong.
resolved-by (full):
**The mechanism embodies the exact error the project has a portable lesson about** — [[LSN-034]]'s refinement, *co-occurrence asserted as membership*. The token list already documents TWO prior false-positive retreats (`committed`, `in progress`), both fixed by DELETING the token: precision-by-subtraction that erodes coverage each time. `deferred` is the third and is a genuine vocabulary word (drafted → GREEN → committed → CLOSED / deferred), so deletion is the wrong fix — **a real fix needs assignment-shape detection.** Canonical source is project-owned (`scripts/ledger_drift_lint.py`, ORCH-004) with a 15-case test file (TEST-017), so it is fixable in-project. **FIXED 2026-08-12 by the orchestrator.** The defect ESCALATED from 1 false positive to **27** — "deferred-deletion semantics" in a WIKI registry line put a status word on a line carrying 20+ ids — making a pre-commit gate unusable and blocking the commit gate regardless of what else landed. `find_statuses()` now applies **assignment-shape discrimination**: a status token immediately followed by a lowercase non-function word is adjectival PROSE, not an assignment ("deferred reaper", "deferred-deletion semantics", "drafted proposal"); punctuation, end-of-line, a table-cell pipe, a capitalised word, or a function word ("DEFERRED to REQ-021") all remain assignments. Deliberately CONSERVATIVE — it suppresses only on that one narrow shape, so the failure mode stays "flags too much", never "misses drift". **Two-directional evidence:** all **15 pre-existing cases still pass** (genuine drift still caught) plus **6 new cases** asserting both directions = **21/21**; **mutation-proven** — forcing `_is_adjectival` to return False restores pure co-occurrence and kills `test_status_word_as_adjective_not_flagged`; restored byte-identical (md5 `2818e086…`, `cmp` clean). Real tree exits 0. **Installed copy SYNCED** via the documented `install_hook.py --extra-hook` and verified byte-identical, since pre-commit and CLV call the installed copy, not `scripts/`.

### ORCH-016 (line 334, Orchestrator/ORCH-015 verification (2026-08-15)) — full pre-compaction record, migrated by librarian Job-3 compaction 2026-09-06
severity (full):

summary (full):
Four residuals, all confirmed by the orchestrator's own 12-line probe. **(i) The citation rule covers PARENTHESES only.** The same false positive still fires when the id is attached by a preposition (`the reaper for DEC-031 is deferred.`), by a possessive (`DEC-031's reaper is deferred.`), or by EM-DASH asides (`the reaper — DEC-031 — is deferred.`) — the last being the most common aside form in these ledgers and therefore the largest hole. Separating a predicate's true subject in the general case needs a parser; the tempting copula heuristic would immediately start MISSING `DEC-031 is deferred.`, which is real drift and structurally indistinguishable. The builder erred toward flagging, consistent with ORCH-010, and wrote the limit into the code comment so the next person inherits it instead of rediscovering it — the right call. **(ii) Object-of-preposition over-report, PRE-DATES ORCH-015:** `REQ-019 (see DEC-024) is DEFERRED to REQ-021` correctly reports REQ-019 and correctly excludes DEC-024, but ALSO reports **REQ-021**, which is the TARGET of "DEFERRED to", not a subject. Needs a different discriminator. Asserted explicitly in the test suite with a comment so it is visible rather than silently tolerated. **(iii) Table-row recall hole from the citation rule:** a row whose only lint-recognised id is a parenthetical citation now goes unflagged. Confirmed on a constructed row carrying a real `GREEN` status cell. On the one REAL instance in the corpus (findings.md:20) the suppression is CORRECT, so this is one data point, not a proof. **(iv) Mutation M10 SURVIVED and the builder declined to fake a kill** — an unclosed `(` extending an aside to EOL changes behavior only for a line where the status precedes an unclosed paren containing the id; pinning it either way would either lock in a false positive of the class just removed or adopt the mutant. Conservative behavior kept, mutant left alive, reasoning recorded.
disposition (full):
**OPEN — non-blocking, NOT scheduled.** No repair is due: the tree lints clean, and (i)'s general case is explicitly a parser problem, not a missing heuristic. This row exists so the next operator hit by a preposition/possessive/em-dash false positive recognizes it as a KNOWN residual with a recorded rationale rather than treating it as a fresh mechanism bug — and, per [[LSN-036]], repairs it rather than routing around it. Em-dash asides are the first place to look. **Do not "fix" (i) with a copula heuristic** — the builder measured that it loses real drift.
resolved-by (full):
Every item here was SELF-DISCLOSED by the builder in its report NOTES, then independently reproduced by the orchestrator on its own probe corpus. The honest surviving mutant (iv) is the item most likely to be mistaken later for sloppiness; it is the opposite. Sibling of ORCH-010/ORCH-015 — same mechanism, same repair-don't-route-around rule.

summary (full):
Found by the adversary, **then reproduced by the orchestrator before anything was recorded**: **CORRECTED MATRIX 2026-08-15 after the diagnosis pass — the first `minimal` datapoint was taken while two agents were saturating the machine and did NOT hold up.** Stable, repeated, idle-machine result, full-suite runs: **ambient wayland session → `47 passed, 2 failed` (BOTH slots, 3/3 runs)** · **`QT_QPA_PLATFORM=minimal` → `48 passed, 1 failed` (the COMMITTED slot only; TEST-102 passes, 4/4 runs, and still passes with all 8 cores under synthetic load)** · **`QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen` → `49 passed, 0 failed`, exit 0**. ENVIRONMENT …)`, so EVERY gate that runs through ctest — the builder's run, the orchestrator's re-run, the CLV, and the clean-worktree build gate — inherited the one backend that hides it. The two failing slots are `anAbortInsideACompletionSlotMustStopTheNextTransfer` (**NEW this slice**, TEST-102) and `completionSlotsStandDownWhenTheAthleteTabDiesInTheirProcessEvents` (**COMMITTED AT HEAD**, REQ-021 wave `6dc794caf`, confirmed present in `git show HEAD:` at :4345). Both fail on the same symptom — a second `readFile` that the guard should have prevented — which points at one shared root: the harness's "deliver a queued action inside the slot's `processEvents()`" trick is not reliably delivered under other backends. **TEST-102's own inline comment (testGarminConnectSyncDialogClose.cpp:513-514) asserts the abort works "by ordering rather than by timing, so nothing here depends on a delay". That claim is measurably false** and is the tell-tale that made the whole finding findable.
disposition (full):
**FIXED 2026-08-15 — gate widened, fixture repaired, orchestrator-verified. F2 CLOSED BY THE SAME FIX (one root cause, two symptoms).** **Phase 1, the gate:** a SECOND ctest registration of the same executable, `testGarminConnectSyncDialogClose_minimal`, under `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=minimal` alongside the untouched `offscreen` one — headless and therefore CI-portable, unlike wayland — with the same `garmin-fast` label so `ctest -L` cannot silently run half the gate. It went RED on the unfixed tree exactly as required (`48 passed, 1 failed`, ctest `50% tests passed`), which is what proves the widening is real. **Phase 2, the fixture:** the action is now delivered through two SYNCHRONOUS seams that code already executing inside the target frame calls directly — `QProgressBar::valueChanged` (emitted by production's own `progressBar->setValue(++downloadcounter)`, which sits strictly downstream of every upstream `aborted` read in all five frames) to anchor the right invocation, then `QAbstractEventDispatcher::awake()`, which `QEventDispatcherGlib` emits UNCONDITIONALLY as its first act on the non-waiting path and therefore independently of what is in the post queue. Measured by standalone probe on all three backends: a bare nested `processEvents()` with NOTHING posted still fires `awake()` exactly once. The two-stage split is not decoration — firing the DESTRUCTIVE teardown at stage 1 would be a fixture-invented UAF, because `QProgressBar::setValue` touches its own d-pointer after emitting and the slots read members two lines later; by `awake()` all of that has happened and the next production statement is the guard. **Orchestrator verification, executed not read:** production `CloudService.{cpp,h}` byte-identical to the pre-task baseline (md5 `704601760b72da2648c44d3b0662063c` / `7eefd7ae78635d12d93919f1fed4e65e`) · ctest both registrations `100% tests passed, 0 failed out of 2` · **ambient wayland full target 49/49 TWICE — the environment where both slots previously failed 3/3** · **my OWN out-of-tree mutations run under WAYLAND: deleting `completedRead`'s abort guard → `readFileCalls == 1` FAILS with the criterion's own message; deleting its `self.isNull()` → `SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free … completedRead`** — so the fixture's mutation sensitivity is now backend-INDEPENDENT, not merely its green runs · goal audit: **zero assertion texts present before the pass and absent after** (mechanical diff of every `QCOMPARE`/`QVERIFY` payload), and the CMakeLists change contains no deleted lines. **Residuals carried to ORCH-017**, not swept up here. Prior disposition (superseded): **BLOCKING — the slice is NOT shippable as it stands, and the disposition is the USER's. DIAGNOSED 2026-08-15: H1, a TEST-HARNESS artifact — the production guard is sound.** `qgdw-builder` instrumented out-of-tree and traced the event order: the harness queues its simulated abort behind the completion and relies on `completedRead`'s `QApplication::processEvents()` to deliver it, but **a nested `processEvents()` is one non-blocking `g_main_context_iteration` and is NOT a guaranteed drain** — whether the Qt post-event source is dispatched in it does not follow from the queue's contents. When the abort does land, the guard reads it and stops the batch at 1 read, every time. **The decisive counterfactual, saved in the builder's logs and re-checked by the orchestrator:** forcing `QCoreApplication::sendPostedEvents(nullptr, 0)` immediately before that `processEvents()` turns the completedRead site green and moves the failure to `failedRead` — the next site with the same fixture shape — proving the event was queued and reachable the whole time. Two obvious rival explanations were REFUTED by measurement (posting an unrelated `QEvent::User` inside the slot; `wakeUp()` on the dispatcher) and "different dispatcher class" was ruled out — both plugins use `QPAEventDispatcherGlib`. **INHERITED, not introduced — orchestrator-verified independently by running the builder's HEAD build myself: `offscreen` 42/0, `minimal` 41/1 failing exactly `completionSlotsStandDown…`.** The working-tree slice adds one NEW backend-sensitive failure (TEST-102) and inherits one. **The H2-flavoured residual that survives and is NOT a test fix:** since `processEvents()` is not a guaranteed drain, DEC-032's guard is best-effort BY CONSTRUCTION — it stops the batch whenever the abort has landed and cannot when it has not. If REQ-027's criterion means "an abort pressed before the next transfer starts must stop it", the placement immune to delivery timing is at the START of the next transfer (before `store->readFile` at `CloudService.cpp:2225`/`:2011` (NOT the `:2220` the production comment at :2367 states — verified at the definition, [[LSN-034]])), not only at the completion slot's tail. That is a DEC-level question and the builder explicitly declined to decide it. Note carefully what is and is not established: a COMMITTED test failing in the default environment means this is at least partly a **pre-existing** condition inherited by this wave, not a regression REQ-027 introduced — our diff only ADDS early-return guards, which can only reduce `readFileCalls`. What is NOT yet established is whether the underlying behaviour is a **test-harness artifact** (the queued-abort delivery trick) or a **production defect** (a guard that genuinely cannot see an abort that has not been delivered yet). Those have very different fixes and the adversary explicitly declined to guess. **Do not "fix" this by pinning the developer's shell to `offscreen`** — that is routing around the mechanism ([[LSN-036]]) and would re-hide exactly what was just found. → [[LSN-062]].
resolved-by (full):
The adversary ran the exact command string from its own briefing rather than the convenient one, which is the entire reason this surfaced; it also correctly reported that its 14/14 mutation matrix, run under `offscreen`, corroborates guard liveness but is ORTHOGONAL to this finding and does not support the 49/49 headline.

The WIKI REGISTRIES line already says findings are tracked as `<cycle>-<seq>` with **no** uniqueness mechanism — unlike REQ/DEC/DES/TEST/VAL/LSN/ORCH, which all allocate from a registry with a `next:`. This is the one id family in the project with no allocator, and it is the one that collided. That is not a coincidence, and it is the same shape as [[LSN-044]] (ORCH-002/003/004 were GUESSED and collided with three existing findings) — which was fixed by giving the ORCH series a registry. → the same fix is available here.

### ORCH-033 (line 361, REQ-028 commit-safety gate (2026-08-22), orchestrator-executed) — full pre-compaction record, migrated by librarian Job-3 compaction 2026-09-06
severity (full):
**BLOCKING — the ASan target does not run to completion in the current working tree, on EITHER backend, and the wave's recorded "78/0 offscreen · green on both backends" is FALSIFIED by execution.**
summary (full):
`heap-use-after-free READ of size 1` at `testGarminConnectSyncDialogClose.cpp:712` in `oracle::TransferOracle::checkConservation`, reached via `checkCompletionRemoval` (:736) ← `BlockingStore::notifyWriteComplete` (:1222) ← `deliverParkedWrite` (:1267) ← the queued lambda at `:5192` inside `runCompletionSlotTeardown`. The freed 456-byte region is the **store itself**, freed by `closeAndDeleteStore<CloudService>` (`CloudService.h:325`) from `~CloudServiceSyncDialog` (`CloudService.cpp:1376`). The lambda at `:5180` captures `dialog` and `store` as **raw pointers**; the teardown armed by `insideframe::atTheNextCountedRow` (:5209) deletes both first, so the delivery runs on a dead store. The oracle is a MEMBER of that store, so it dies with its subject — its `dialog_` is a `QPointer` and survives dialog death, but nothing guards the oracle's own liveness. **Harm is confined to the harness** (production never calls into a store it deleted on this route), but it halts the suite at test 32 of 73 and therefore destroys the wave's acceptance evidence. Deterministic: 4/4 isolated runs, 2 per backend, identical signature.
disposition (full):
**fix-now — blocked the commit gate.** **DIAGNOSIS CORRECTED BY THE USER BEFORE THE REPAIR, and the correction was load-bearing:** the store is ALIVE when the queued delivery begins. It dies *re-entrantly inside* `CloudService::notifyWriteComplete`, because that base call invokes the dialog's completion slot directly, the slot pumps events, and a teardown delivered there destroys the dialog → `~CloudServiceSyncDialog` → `closeAndDeleteStore`. The crash frame is `:1222`, the statement AFTER the base call — which is the proof: a store already dead at entry would never have reached it. My original "the lambda ran on an already-dead store" named the wrong window and would have produced a fix that did not hold.
resolved-by (full):
**RESOLVED 2026-08-22, commit `e48f7d123`.** Two windows guarded in `testGarminConnectSyncDialogClose.cpp` only: (1) a `QPointer` self-guard across each of `notifyReadComplete`/`notifyReadFailed`/`notifyWriteComplete`, with nothing touched through `this` once it is null; (2) `QPointer` handles on the queued delivery's captures so a callback posted after an earlier teardown is a no-op. One narrow consequence handled honestly rather than papered over: where the observer is destroyed by the delivery it observes, the post-removal resample is IMPOSSIBLE, not skipped — recorded in namespace scope as `observerDestroyedInDelivery` so the `completionRemovalSamples` meta-invariant distinguishes that from an oracle that simply stopped looking, which still fails. **Evidence:** full target **78 passed / 0 failed / 0 sanitizer summaries, EXIT=0** on BOTH backends (73 declared functions + init/cleanup + data rows = 78 QtTest total); both ctest registrations Passed; `ctest -L garmin-fast` 25/25, covering the 23 other targets compiling the shared `ImportSeamStubs.cpp` ([[LSN-056]]). **Mutation:** removing ONLY the `notifyWriteComplete` self-guard reproduced the original signature (`:726 in checkConservation`) on both backends; restored byte-identically, `cmp` clean. Production `CloudService.{cpp,h}` md5-unchanged throughout.

disposition (full):

### ORCH-027 (line 406, Orchestrator/DEC-036 briefing (2026-08-18)) — full pre-compaction record, migrated by librarian Job-3 compaction 2026-09-06
severity (full):
non-blocking — **A FINDING THAT IS ABOUT TO DRIVE A DEC CARRIED A FALSE PREMISE ABOUT THE SIGNAL SIGNATURE, AND IT WOULD HAVE NARROWED THE OPTION SPACE.** B-R028-03 states *"the completion carries no identity of its own: `completedWrite` has no payload"*. `writeComplete` has carried a payload since it was written.
summary (full):
Verified by Grep while assembling the DEC-036 briefing: `CloudService.h:243` declares `void writeComplete(QString id, QString message);` and `CloudService.h:139` `notifyWriteComplete(QString name, QString message)`. The slot `CloudServiceSyncDialog::completedWrite` (`CloudService.cpp:2831`) leaves its first parameter **unnamed** and discards it — which is where the "no payload" reading came from. **What is actually true, and it is a different claim:** the id is emitted but is not usable as identity on every service — `LocalFileStore.cpp:163/170/179/183` emits `writeComplete("", …)`, while `Strava.cpp:506`, `SportTracks.cpp:594`, `CyclingAnalytics.cpp:535`, `RideWithGPS.cpp:256` and `Selfloops.cpp:191` all pass `replyName(sender())`. On the read half the buffer pointer (`new QByteArray` at `downloadNext:2382` and its `syncNext` twin, passed through to both `readComplete` and `readFailed`) IS a genuine per-transfer token.
disposition (full):
**CORRECTED IN B-R028-03 IN PLACE 2026-08-18, before the scout was dispatched; the corrected version went into the briefing.** OPEN as a process finding, non-blocking.
resolved-by (full):
**"The wire carries no identity" and "the slot throws the identity away" are opposite defects with opposite fixes** — the first needs a signature change across ~16 services, the second needs one slot to name its parameter. The measurement here — TEST-107 still green after the fix — was and remains correct.

### S-R028-01 (line 411, Scout/DEC-034 (2026-08-16)) — full pre-compaction record, migrated by librarian Job-3 compaction 2026-09-06
severity (full):
blocking — **A THIRD LIST MUTATOR THAT NO FINDING, REQ OR DEC HAS EVER NAMED: SORTING. It is invisible to every guard proposed for REQ-028 — a re-sort frees nothing, so `refreshButton` gating cannot see it, `batchGeneration` cannot see it, and a list-generation counter cannot see it.**
summary (full):
**Orchestrator-confirmed by grepping every `setSortingEnabled` in the file.** All three lists are constructed sorting-ENABLED (`:1116` `rideListDown`, `:1146` `rideListUp`, `:1186` `rideListSync`). At batch start `downloadClicked` disables sorting on `rideListDown` **only** (`:1920`) and **explicitly ENABLES it on `rideListUp`** (`:1921`); **`rideListSync` is never disabled anywhere** — every one of its `setSortingEnabled` calls in the file passes `true` (:1186, :2237). The abort branch re-enables Down and Up at :1911/:1912. So during a Sync batch the list being iterated is sorting-enabled the whole time, and during an Upload batch `rideListUp` is *deliberately* re-enabled. A column-header click delivered from inside the same nested loops that already deliver a Refresh would REORDER items without freeing them — breaking the positional `child(listindex-1)` addressing in all three completion slots (:2388/:2437/:2444/:2525/:2532/:2717/:2724) and the `for (i=listindex; …)` walk in all three drivers. Not a UAF: a wrong-row-labelled / row-skipped / row-processed-twice defect of the same family.
disposition (full):
**fixed — dispositioned 2026-09-01 BY EXECUTION, to the [[ORCH-050]] bar (verify first, then transcribe).** **The measure-then-decide order this row demanded was followed, and the measurement came back against Option C's silence: sorting WAS a live third list mutator, and DEC-038 turned it off for the batch's duration.** The mechanism is in CURRENT source (re-located, because this row's own cites `:1116/:1146/:1186` are stale — sorting is enabled at **`:1430/:1460/:1500`** today): the guard pair is headed `// DEC-garmin-038 (= DEC-garmin-034 AMENDMENT, S-R028-01/S-R028-02) - SORTING IS OFF FOR THE BATCH'S DURATION` at **`CloudService.cpp:1851`**, disabling all three lists at **`:1885`** and restoring each list's own recorded column+order at **`:1949`**; it is armed from the one place a batch starts at **`:2395`** (*"A BATCH STARTS HERE, SO SORTING STOPS HERE, ON ALL THREE LISTS"*), and released at the three drivers' tails **`:2988`, `:3121`, `:3736`**. That comment also records the defect this row named, measured: *"the sync and upload drivers walked lists that reordered underneath them on every status write they made (TEST-131 Q5c: the same row uploaded twice, the other never)"*. **The three-driver guard family was RE-RUN 2026-09-01 at `37710370e`** (gauntlet-build; `ninja` no work to do) under `ASAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1:detect_leaks=0`: `aPreBatchStatusSortMustNotMakeSyncNextTransferARowTwice` (:13497), `…UploadNextTransferARowTwice` (:13530) and `…DownloadNextTransferARowTwice` (:13559) each **3 passed / 0 failed / EXIT=0 on BOTH `offscreen` AND `minimal`** — six runs, all green. Closure authority: `traceability.md:341` — the DEC-038 slice, *"Closes S-R028-01 and S-R028-02 (the sort route)"*, committed **`514d8e88f`**. **ROUTING: DISCHARGED** — the gap this row's own routing note recorded (*"DEC-038 later suspends list sorting, but no row records that as this finding's disposition"*) is closed here, on executed evidence. **Scope note, deliberate:** that same `traceability.md:341` line also closes `B-R028-05`'s DRIVER half, which is NOT dispositioned here — `B-R028-05` has a second (labelling) half under DEC-036 and keeps its own row. The `BLOCKS: {TASK:REQ-028}` set is left unchanged — an effect set is an independent axis and never moved this row's disposition. **PRIOR DISPOSITION (Gate 1A/1B, 2026-08-30), preserved VERBATIM and now SUPERSEDED:** OPEN — USER DECISION 2026-08-17: TRACE ITS REACHABILITY INSIDE REQ-028 PHASE 2 (TEST-112) BEFORE DECIDING WHETHER IT REOPENS DEC-034. This reverses the 2026-08-16 "track, not fold in" — but not into a fold-in, because folding it in as a binding constraint **would falsify DEC-034 Option C by construction**: Option C is positional addressing plus a counter, a re-sort bumps no counter and frees nothing, and of the three shapes researched **only value/key addressing survives a reorder**, being the only one independent of a row's POSITION and of the container's identity. That makes it a DEC REOPEN (the DEC-031-reopens-DEC-025 pattern), not a scope tweak — and a reopen resting on a route recorded *"reasoned, not traced"* would be an inference deciding a decision. **So the order is: measure, then decide.** If TEST-112 reorders, DEC-034 reopens with EXECUTED evidence; if the click cannot be delivered, the slot is recorded undrivable with its reason and Option C stands unchallenged. Phase 2 meanwhile builds Option C as accepted, so the BLOCKING null-deref is not held hostage to this. **Narrowed while briefing (2026-08-17), and it makes the route look reachable: nothing in the file calls `setSectionsClickable(false)`, and Qt's `setSortingEnabled(true)` — called on all three lists at :1116/:1146/:1186 — makes header sections clickable as part of its contract. REASONED FROM THE API CONTRACT, NOT EXECUTED ([[LSN-063]]), and deliberately left as TEST-112's job rather than promoted to a claim: this ledger has had exactly that class of framework-semantics inference falsified by measurement twice (TEST-081, TEST-089).** **[Gate 1B 2026-08-30] BLOCKS: {TASK:REQ-028}** — effect set read off this row's OWN recorded harm; scope PROVEN, not assumed, so it names the raising task and not a global block. Routing: UNROUTED — raised against REQ-028, which is TEST VERIFIED / COMMITTED; DEC-038 later suspends list sorting, but no row records that as this finding's disposition.
resolved-by (full):
**REASONED FROM CODE, NOT TRACED** — the scout explicitly declined to claim the route, because it did not confirm the column header is user-clickable in this dialog's layout, and per [[LSN-063]] a guard's reachability needs a trace, not an inference. **SHARPENED 2026-08-16 while verifying TEST-107's P1 at Qt's source, and it makes this finding harder rather than easier:** `QTreeWidgetItem::child(int)` (`qtreewidget.h:145-150`) calls **`executePendingSort()`** before returning the item. Qt's sorting is therefore LAZY — a pending re-sort is applied *at the moment of the addressing call itself*. So the reorder does not merely happen "sometime between capture and use": it can be executed **inside the very `child(listindex-1)` expression** the completion slots use, which means no guard placed *around* that expression can observe the list in its pre-sort order. Any Phase-2 design that assumes "check the container, then address it" has a window it cannot close on this route. That refusal is correct and is why this is a finding rather than a REQ. The wider point: [[LSN-060]] said the suspension set must include the ROW, and this shows the enumeration is *still* incomplete — the row can be invalidated by REORDERING, not only by destruction, and every axis on record assumed destruction.

not-a-defect — Found while explaining why mutation M9 (dropping the `if (!sortingSuspended) return;` early-out in `restoreListSorting()`) killed TEST-112. **NOT A LIVE DEFECT — the shipped code makes every enable a real transition, so the state is never entered.** Recorded because the property is FRAGILE and nothing but the `sortingSuspended` guard enforces it: any future caller that enables sorting on an already-sorting list re-arms this. **This is what makes the M9 early-out load-bearing for a reason the decision never anticipated** — it was written as idempotence hygiene, and it turns out to be the thing standing between this codebase and a guard that reads as ON while the vector is OPEN.  **[overflow col 7 — preserved verbatim; see 'ROW OVERFLOW' in this file's header]** Worth an adversary's attention: `isSortingEnabled()` returning false is the assertion nearly every new slot rests on, and this finding says that reading can be a LIE in a state reachable by one redundant call. Whether any OTHER path can make a redundant enable was not enumerated — the builder closed only the M9 route.

summary (full):
`git stash list` → a single entry, `stash@{0}: On master: non-garmin WIP — Coach/Seasons/RideFile/Gui/Train, stashed during REQ-002 RED (qgw workflow)`, based on `6381b90f4` (2026-05-23, "feat(cloud): add Garmin Connect tile-contract subclass (REQ-001)"). Contents: 18 files, +651/-53 — `src/Coach/GCToolExecutor.{cpp,h}`, `GeminiClient.{cpp,h}`, `ToolConfirmCard.cpp`, `src/Core/Seasons.{cpp,h}`, `src/FileIO/RideFile.{cpp,h}`, `src/Gui/{AbstractView.h,MainWindow.cpp,MainWindow.h,NewSideBar.h,Perspective.h}`, `src/Resources/application.qrc`, `src/Train/KurtInRide.cpp`, `.vscode/settings.json`, and `unittests/Core/coach/testCoachTools.cpp` (+472). **Two facts establish it is not redundant, both verified read-only:** (1) `GCToolExecutor.cpp`, `GCToolExecutor.h`, `Seasons.cpp`, `RideFile.cpp` and `testCoachTools.cpp` are all CLEAN in today's working tree — the stash's changes to them are present nowhere on disk; (2) the stash's blob for each of those four differs from HEAD's. Determining that needs the Coach owner, not an inference.
disposition (full):
**OPEN — reported, NOT acted on. Explicitly the user's call.** Nothing was popped, applied, dropped or branched; the stash is untouched and the working tree is unchanged. The safe inspection route if the user wants one is `git stash show -p stash@{0}` or `git stash branch <name> stash@{0}`, which creates a branch from the stash's own base and leaves `master` alone. **Do NOT `git stash pop` onto the current tree** — it carries 54 dirty entries of the same owners' newer work and a conflicting pop would interleave three-month-old edits with live ones.
resolved-by (full):
Every prior wave's housekeeping note has carefully enumerated the dirty working-tree entries as "other owners' pre-session churn" and left them alone, which is right — but no wave ever looked in the stash, so a second, older, invisible pile of the same owners' work sat outside that accounting the whole time. The lesson is about the SHAPE of the blind spot: the housekeeping question was always framed as "what is dirty?", and `git status` cannot answer "what is stashed?". → candidate lesson: **an inventory of uncommitted work is incomplete until it has looked at the stash, the reflog, and any other worktrees** — the same class as the clean-worktree gate, which exists because every other gate ran inside the developer's tree.

summary (full):
Every one of the four call sites into `syncNext()`/`downloadNext()` re-establishes `aborted == false` in the same statement block, with nothing that pumps events in between: `completedRead` checks at `:2435` and calls at `:2438`/`:2440`; `failedRead` checks at `:2495` and calls at `:2498`/`:2500`; `completedWrite` checks at `:2689` and calls at `:2692`; `downloadClicked` assigns `aborted=false` at `:1923` and calls at `:1969`/`:1971`. The only in-function loop continuation that crosses a suspension, `syncNext`'s `continue` at `:2195`, is itself preceded by `if (aborted == true) return true;` at `:2186` and the batch-generation re-check at `:2193`. `downloadNext`'s other `continue` (`:2242`, the File-exists branch) crosses nothing that pumps. **Orchestrator spot-check: all four call sites and both continue paths opened and CONFIRMED at their cited lines.** The adversary proved the other half by mutation: neutralising `:2030` leaves 50/51 with TEST-105 the sole failure on its own criterion `readFileCalls == 0`; neutralising `:2268` gives the identical result for TEST-106; nothing else in the suite moves either way.
disposition (full):
**OPEN — non-blocking. Its REACHABILITY CLAIM is ACCEPTED; its proposed REMEDY is REJECTED, and the distinction matters more than the finding.** The adversary recommends relabelling both guards in the `UNTESTED-BY-DESIGN` vocabulary the adjacent `self.isNull()` guards use (`:2060`, `:2288`). **That would be less accurate than what is there now, and actively dangerous.** The two unreachabilities are not the same kind: the `self.isNull()` guards are unreachable because nothing can destroy the dialog in their window — a LOCAL property, checkable by reading fifteen lines. The DEC-035 guards are unreachable because four REMOTE call sites each happen to re-check — a DISTRIBUTED invariant no reader of `syncNext` can verify, and one that any future fifth caller silently breaks. That is precisely what DEC-035's own comment already calls a "true-by-luck arrangement … it holds only as long as every route into this loop happens to have read `aborted` on the way", so the code is not claiming a live reachable gap and F1 does not catch it doing so. Filing both guards under the same label as genuinely dead code invites exactly the deletion the guard exists to survive. **Agreed remediation instead:** state the reachability status explicitly and name its nature — no production route reaches these with `aborted` set TODAY; the guard converts a distributed invariant into a local one so that a future caller which omits the re-check cannot reintroduce the defect — and say plainly that TEST-105/106 are therefore regression locks on a local invariant, not proofs of a live fix.
resolved-by (full):
Note what this cycle did NOT overturn, because it is the reason the wave ran: DEC-035's premise was that `QApplication::processEvents()` is not a guaranteed drain and the completion-slot guard is best-effort BY CONSTRUCTION. F1 does not touch that premise — it establishes that the CURRENT set of callers happens to leave no gap, which is a statement about today's four call sites, not about the delivery semantics. Sibling of [[LSN-055]] on the report side: the adversary's defect was accepted and its mechanism was not.

### B-R027-01 (line 432, Builder/REQ-027 (2026-08-13)) — full pre-compaction record, migrated by librarian Job-3 compaction 2026-09-06
severity (full):
**BLOCKING for scope item 3 — the briefing's central premise about `readFile`'s bool is FALSE, and building to it would have shipped a silent double-drive across ~11 integrations. Builder refused to write any code and cited the falsifying command. ORCHESTRATOR RE-RAN IT AND CONFIRMED.**
summary (full):
The briefing (and the scout's F1, and O-R027-01 as first recorded) claimed "every real implementation returns false only on paths that armed nothing", citing `GarminConnect.cpp:451-452`. **`GarminConnect::readFile` (defined :449) has EIGHT `return false` sites — 452, 474, 493, 519, 540, 557, 572, 588 — and SEVEN post a completion on the line immediately above** (:472, :492, :516, :537, :554, :569, :587). Both `postReadComplete` (:765-770) and `postReadFailed` (:780-785) use `Qt::QueuedConnection`, so the emission lands **after** the false return, delivered by `syncNext`'s own `processEvents` (:2012) or `downloadNext`'s (:2144). Only :452 (`data == nullptr || m_client == nullptr`) is genuinely silent — the one site the orchestrator sampled. So `false` does NOT mean "armed nothing": on GarminConnect it usually means "armed something, deferred". A label-advance-continue branch would run the bar forward synchronously **and then again** when the queued completion arrives, with `completedRead`/`failedRead` labelling `child(listindex-1)` — a different row by then — and re-driving the loop, leaving two drivers on one list. **This is the same double-drive the briefing correctly forbade for `writeFile`, and it regresses DEC-022/023**, whose stated design is "post a labelled completion carrying the still-empty buffer and still return false: the loop moves on" (`GarminConnect.cpp:462-470`).
disposition (full):
**fixed 2026-09-04 — was: open.** **SCOPE ITEM 3 (O-R027-01) IS PULLED OUT OF REQ-027 and routed to DEC-033.** It is not fixable inside `syncNext`/`downloadNext`: `readFile` hands back a bare bool and the callee never communicates "returned false AND armed nothing", which is exactly what criterion (e) was phrased against. Resolution needs a governance choice with no governing DEC — widen the contract (tri-state / out-param) across ~11 overrides, or make GarminConnect return true where it emitted (touches REQ-017/023 and their tests), or a deferred watchdog. Builder correctly refused to pick. **[Gate 1B 2026-08-30] BLOCKS: {TASK:DEC-033}** — effect set read off this row's OWN recorded harm; scope PROVEN, not assumed, so it names the raising task and not a global block. Routing: routed -> STATE.md Stage 2 (this row pulls scope item 3 out of REQ-027 and routes it to DEC-033, which is ALLOCATED with no entry). **CLOSED 2026-09-04.** DEC-033 BUILT (Option A): `syncNext`/`downloadNext` both read the out-param instead of discarding the bool. Verified by execution: `T-155(a)`/`T-156(a)` RED-before/GREEN-after on the criterion's own assertion (`out.readFileCalls == 2`, i.e. the batch now attempts the next row instead of stalling); orchestrator independently reproduced the base suite (97 slots) twice and re-ran the DEC-033 alignment probe directly against source.
resolved-by (full):
Sixth briefing-premise failure, sixth caught by the hatch, and the first that would have been a **silent production regression** rather than a test failure. → [[LSN-034]] recur:6, and the reason mechanism promotion is now overdue.

summary (full):

But the **base** `CloudService::readFile` (`CloudService.h:142-144`) is `{ return false; }` — it emits **neither** signal. A Download-capable service that does not override `readFile` therefore stalls the batch at those sites in exactly the B-R026-01 shape. Enumerated by matching the predicate itself rather than by proximity ([[LSN-034]] refinement 1): across services declaring `Download` explicitly (`Azum`, `Nolio`, `CyclingAnalytics`, `Withings`, `GarminConnect`, `PolarFlow`) and those inheriting the `CloudService.h:104` default (`Strava`, `Dropbox`, `SixCycle`, `SportTracks`, `LocalFileStore`), **`Withings` alone (`Withings.h:43` = `OAuth | Download`) overrides neither `readFile` nor `readdir`** — verified by opening `Withings.h`/`Withings.cpp`, not by subtracting two greps.
disposition (full):
**fixed — dispositioned 2026-09-06 BY EXECUTION, to the [[ORCH-050]] bar (verify first, then transcribe); the last Stage-2 row, transcribed one session late.** The stall class this row raised — a `readFile` that returns false having armed nothing, so nothing re-drives the batch — is closed at the LOOP level by DEC-033 (Option A, the `ArmedNothing`/`ArmedCompletion` out-param), COMMITTED `2e26106c1`: `syncNext`/`downloadNext` now read the out-param and advance instead of stalling, which covers BOTH populations this row enumerated — the error-path overriders (`LocalFileStore`, `Strava`, `Dropbox`, `Xert`, `SportTracks`, `CyclingAnalytics`, `PolarFlow`, `Nolio`, `SixCycle`, `GarminConnect`) and the override-nothing Download declarer (`Withings`) — because the guard reads the out-param at the loop, not at any site, and the genuinely-silent site's `ArmedNothing` report is itself pinned by TEST-154. RE-EXECUTED 2026-09-06, this session, on the current working tree with a fresh build (`ninja`: no work to do): `ctest` over the three DEC-033 binaries — `testGarminConnectReadFile` + `testGarminConnectReadFailure` + `testGarminConnectRefusalCompletion` — **3/3 binaries PASSED, EXIT=0** (the T-154 armed-reporting slots; ReadFailure's stall slots, whose own comment reads "that stall IS the defect"; RefusalCompletion's slots, whose file header reads "readFile() REPORTS itself instead of stalling the sync loop"). Sibling rows `B-R027-01/02/03` closed 2026-09-04 on the same build; this row's transcription was missed at Stage-2 close, flagged in STATE.md `## BLOCKING`, and is now reconciled — with it, Stage 2's finding set is complete. The `BLOCKS: {TASK:DEC-033}` effect is left unchanged — an effect set is an independent axis and never moved this row's disposition. **PRIOR DISPOSITION (2026-08-13, corrected same day; carried through Gate 1B 2026-08-30), preserved VERBATIM and now SUPERSEDED:** **OPEN — LIVE, not dormant. CORRECTED 2026-08-13 by the scout (S-R027-05) and re-verified by the orchestrator; the original disposition below was WRONG and is kept visible rather than overwritten.** ~~"DORMANT … not reachable today: base `readdir` (`CloudService.h:205-207`) returns an empty list, so no download row can ever be built for `Withings`."~~ That reasoning scoped the hazard to services with **no `readFile` override**, and so missed the larger population: **the services that DO override `readFile` also return `false` without emitting, on their ordinary error paths.** Orchestrator-verified in `LocalFileStore::readFile` — `path == ""` → `return false`, `!current_path.exists()` → `return false`, **`!file.exists()` → `return false`**, `open()` failure → `return false`, and the sole `emit readComplete` sits AFTER all four. So a file listed by `readdir` and deleted before download stalls the whole batch **today, with no code change and no new service**. Same shape at `Strava.cpp:270`, `Dropbox.cpp:232/236`, `Xert.cpp:344`, `SportTracks.cpp:261`, `CyclingAnalytics.cpp:261`, `PolarFlow.cpp:177`, `Nolio.cpp:212-213`, `SixCycle.cpp:319-320`, `GarminConnect.cpp:451-452` (cleared/absent token). **This changes the disposition from "accept-or-close" to CLOSE**, and it is the [[LSN-048]] lesson recurring against the orchestrator's own re-derivation: I enumerated the population by "who lacks an override" when the predicate was "who can return false without emitting". Read side only — see S-R027-02 for why `writeFile`'s bool must stay discarded. **[Gate 1B 2026-08-30] BLOCKS: {TASK:DEC-033}** — effect set read off this row's OWN recorded harm; scope PROVEN, not assumed, so it names the raising task and not a global block. Routing: routed -> STATE.md Stage 2 (STATE.md Stage 2 already names this row as governed by DEC-033).
resolved-by (full):
The stall class is not "one bad branch" but "any path that returns without arming a re-entry point" — [[LSN-057]]'s rule stated at the seam level rather than the branch level. Sibling axis of [[LSN-041]] (other objects) / [[LSN-048]] (other frames).

### S-R028f-F1 (line 465, Sweep/F2 sibling-provider boundedness (2026-08-26)) — full pre-compaction record, migrated by librarian Job-3 compaction 2026-09-06
summary (full):
**NINE OF THE SEVENTEEN REACHABLE CloudService PROVIDERS BLOCK IN A `QEventLoop` WITH NO WATCHDOG — so a join-based teardown of `CloudServiceAutoDownload` has NO finite worst case.** All 17 subclasses are reachable: `run():3650` iterates every `CloudServiceFactory::instance().serviceNames()` entry and admits any whose per-athlete `syncstartup` value is `"true"`, and `syncOnStartupSettingName()` is defined on the BASE class (`CloudService.h:258`), so each service is independently togglable. Twelve participate in the download path. **BOUNDED:** GarminConnect (`kRestoreTimeoutMs` 30000 / `kDownloadTimeoutMs` 60000 / `kListTimeoutMs` 60000 at `GarminConnect.cpp:41-43`, plus a ≤2.5s `close()` via the chain dtor) · SixCycle (`SixCycle.cpp:118` 5000ms and `:244` 10000ms, both armed BEFORE `loop.exec()`) · LocalFileStore (local filesystem, no nested loop). **UNBOUNDED:** Dropbox · Azum · SportTracks · Xert · Nolio · PolarFlow · Strava · TrainingsTageBuch (`open()` only) — each constructs a `QEventLoop`, connects only `reply::finished()` to `quit()`, and calls `exec()` with no timer. **UNBOUNDED VIA A LATENT BUG:** CyclingAnalytics (see [[S-R028f-F3]]). **NO DOWNLOAD PATH / NO BLOCKING WAIT:** RideWithGPS · CalDAVCloud · Selfloops · SportsPlusHealth · Withings (zero `::readdir`/`::readFile` definitions). `close()` is trivial for 16 of 17 — only GarminConnect overrides it — so the teardown half is bounded and the IN-FLIGHT-OPERATION half is not.
disposition (full):
**OPEN — non-blocking characterisation. BLOCKS: {}.** User disposition 2026-08-26. **This finding REFUTES a quantity this workflow had itself asserted:** the orchestrator's earlier "worst-case join ≈ 2.5s × P" covered only provider TEARDOWN and silently omitted the in-flight operation the join must wait through. With any of the nine enabled, worst-case join time is unbounded, not 2.5s × P. **Consequence, already acted on:** the Option-3 blocking-join intermediate is REJECTED and F2's design is cooperative cancellation plus GUI-thread owner-teardown deferral, which tolerates an unbounded worker because the owner graph stays alive until `finished()` is observed. Adding watchdogs to the nine is a SEPARATE class-wide slice ([[LSN-041]] shape, shared base contract) and explicitly does NOT gate the deferral design.

### S-R028f-F2 (line 466, Sweep/F2 sibling-provider boundedness (2026-08-26)) — full pre-compaction record, migrated by librarian Job-3 compaction 2026-09-06
summary (full):
**AN EXTERNAL `QThread::quit()` CANNOT BE USED TO BOUND THE WORKER, BECAUSE IT TURNS AN UNFINISHED REPLY INTO A FALSE SUCCESS AND LEAKS IT.** The orchestrator's own probe (Qt 6.8.2, ASan, exit 0) established that `quit()` interrupts a LOCAL nested `QEventLoop` on a thread whose overridden `run()` never called `QThread::exec()` (199ms vs a 3139ms no-quit control), and that the exit request LATCHES so subsequent local loops return immediately (0ms). **What the probe did NOT establish, and this sweep did:** what the collapsed frames then do. Every unbounded provider follows Strava's shape (`Strava.cpp:116-127`) — `loop.exec();` then `reply->attribute(QNetworkRequest::HttpStatusCodeAttribute)` and `if (reply->error() != 0)`, with **nothing checking that the reply actually finished**. Under a latch-driven early return the reply is still in flight, so `statusCode` is 0 and `error()` is `NoError`: the provider proceeds as though an empty response SUCCEEDED, and the `QNetworkReply` is never deleted. The identical shape appears in Dropbox (`:121`, `:169`), Azum, SportTracks, Xert, Nolio and PolarFlow.
disposition (full):
**OPEN — non-blocking characterisation. BLOCKS: {}.** User disposition 2026-08-26, carried directly into F2's decision constraints: **cancellation must set a thread-safe stop request checked only at safe worklist/download boundaries, and must NOT call `QThread::quit()` while a provider may be inside its own `QEventLoop`.** This is the concrete form of the "the inner chains unwind for free" hazard the user flagged: the unwind is prompt, but promptness is bought with silent data corruption. The synchronous fast path is therefore permitted only when `finished()`/`wait(0)` PROVES `run()` has returned, never when a latch merely made the loops return.
resolved-by (full):
Found while establishing whether `quit()` could rescue the bound that [[S-R028f-F1]] destroyed. Notable as a case where an EXECUTED probe answered its own question correctly and was still over-generalised by the orchestrator — the measurement was sound, the inference from it was not. Same family as [[LSN-053]] (a mutation/measurement result means exactly what it observed, and no more).

### S-R028f-F3 (line 467, Sweep/F2 sibling-provider boundedness (2026-08-26)) — full pre-compaction record, migrated by librarian Job-3 compaction 2026-09-06
summary (full):
**`CyclingAnalytics` ARMS ITS ADVERTISED 30-SECOND TIMEOUT AFTER THE LOOP IT IS SUPPOSED TO BOUND HAS ALREADY RETURNED — the watchdog is dead code and the wait is unbounded.** `CyclingAnalytics.cpp:128-132`: the comment reads `// blocking request, with a 30s timeout`, then `QEventLoop loop; connect(reply, SIGNAL(finished()), &loop, SLOT(quit())); loop.exec();` and only THEN `QTimer::singleShot(30000,&loop, SLOT(quit())); // timeout after 30 seconds`. The single-shot is armed against a loop that has already exited, so it can never fire usefully; the only exit from `exec()` is `reply::finished()`, which a hung connection never delivers. Contrast `SixCycle.cpp:116-120` and `:242-246`, which arm the same idiom in the CORRECT order and are genuinely bounded.
disposition (full):
**OPEN — non-blocking, PRE-EXISTING production defect, unrelated to REQ-028's changeset. BLOCKS: {}.** User disposition 2026-08-26. Repairing it belongs to the SEPARATE class-wide provider-watchdog slice alongside [[S-R028f-F1]]'s eight genuinely watchdog-less providers, NOT to F2's deferral design, which does not gate on it. Recorded now so the next reader inherits a measured fact rather than trusting the comment.
resolved-by (full):
Found by verifying whether the two providers that appeared to have timers actually bounded their waits, rather than counting `QTimer` occurrences and calling them watchdogs. The comment asserting a 30s timeout is precisely the kind of stale in-source claim that [[LSN-045]] exists for — a future reader auditing boundedness by reading comments would score this provider as safe.

### C4 (line 471, Census/provider-watchdog design gate (2026-08-26)) — full pre-compaction record, migrated by librarian Job-3 compaction 2026-09-06
summary (full):
**NO PROVIDER ABORTS OR DELETES ANY `QNetworkReply` — THERE IS NO CANCELLATION MECHANISM ANYWHERE IN `src/Cloud/`.** `grep -e "abort()" src/Cloud/*.cpp` returns **ZERO hits**; `grep -c "deleteLater|delete reply"` over Azum, CyclingAnalytics, Dropbox, Nolio, PolarFlow, SportTracks, Strava, TrainingsTageBuch and Xert returns **0 for every one of the nine**. Consequences: (1) a timeout cannot stop the underlying request — the socket stays open and the transfer continues after the caller has given up; (2) replies are released only when the provider's `nam` is destroyed (`Strava.cpp:58` `new QNetworkAccessManager(this)`, `:75` `if (context) delete nam;`), so within one long `readdir` they accumulate for the whole listing; (3) any bounded-wait design must INTRODUCE disposal, because there is no existing convention to extend.

BLOCKS: {} NOW; CHECKPOINT effect DISCHARGED (was `{CHECKPOINT:provider-watchdog slice}`).** User disposition 2026-08-26 made reply ownership a first-class term of the helper contract. Discharged by the shared `ReplyDisposer` (`src/Cloud/CloudService.cpp:182-211`, anonymous-namespace RAII wrapping `blockingRequest`'s `reply`) plus T-145's 22-site coverage. `ReplyDisposer::dispose()` (`:197-203`) is exactly the contract this row asked for: `if (!reply_->isFinished()) reply_->abort();` then `reply_->deleteLater();`, invoked exactly once — BY NAME at STEP 3 (`:395`), not merely at scope exit — with STEP 4 (`:398-421`) asserting via a `qFatal` invariant that nothing moved underneath that disposal. T-145 (`site_replyDestroyedExactlyOnce`, `testCloudProviderWatchdog.cpp:1787-1818`) drives every one of the 22 sites through THREE outcome paths (responding/silent/errored) and asserts `net::repliesDestroyed == net::repliesCreated - skip` and every issued reply `.isNull()` afterward — a real per-site production-call-site row, not a helper-only assertion. **Orchestrator independently re-executed 2026-09-05** (this session, fresh rebuild, `ninja: no work to do` beforehand): 168 passed/0 failed both backends, EXIT=0, zero ASan; full `ctest -L garmin-fast` **27/27 passed, EXIT=0, 259.35s**. ### ORCH-043 (line 474, Orchestrator/DEC-040 Stage-1 dispatch (2026-08-26)) — full pre-compaction record, migrated by librarian Job-3 compaction 2026-09-06
summary (full):
**THE ANTI-DUPLICATION GUARD PARSED A READ-ONLY `grep` FLAG CLUSTER AS A FILE-CLOBBERING BINARY, AND IT AFFECTED FOUR VERBS, NOT ONE.** The verb regexes were anchored `\b<verb>\b`. In `grep -ln PATTERN FILE` the `-` is a non-word character, so `\bln\b` matched the FLAG CLUSTER `-ln`; the guard then treated the last path on the line as an `ln` link name and DENIED the grep as a clobber. **Reproduced in isolation before any repair** (direct regex probe, then the guard end-to-end on a fixture project): `grep -ln … src/Cloud/SixCycle.h` denied; `grep -rln …` NOT denied, because the `r` supplies a word char and kills the boundary; `ln -sf a b` correctly denied. So the defect is precisely a cluster that BEGINS with the verb right after the dash AND ENDS there — `-ln` reproduces, `-lni` does not — which is why the common `-rln` spelling hid it for so long. **The two-directional matrix then showed the blast radius was wider than reported: `grep -cp`, `grep -mv` and `grep -tee` were denied too. Four verbs.**
disposition (full):
**CLOSED 2026-08-26 by a bounded mechanism repair — and the repair is EVIDENCED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, which is what ORCH-040 asked for and never got.** `_CMD_POS = r"(?<![-\w])"` replaces the left `\b` on the mkdir/touch/tee/cp|mv/ln verb regexes in `.claude/hooks/anti_duplication_guard.py:158-173`; fixed-width lookbehind, so it still succeeds at string start, and `/usr/bin/ln` (preceded by `/`) and `$(ln …)` (preceded by `(`) still match. **Matrix `scripts/test_anti_duplication_guard_flags.py`, 15 cases: 15 PASS / EXIT=0 on the repaired guard, and 4 FAIL / EXIT=4 on the pre-repair snapshot — so the matrix demonstrably DISCRIMINATES rather than merely passing ([[LSN-050]]).** All SEVEN genuine-clobber cases (`ln`, `ln -s`, `ln -f`, `ln -sf`, `/usr/bin/ln -sf`, `cp`, `mv` over an existing mapped file) were DENIED in BOTH versions — direct evidence the repair removed a false positive without weakening a real guard. The bundled `guard_selftest.py` re-run on the repaired hook: **0 core, 0 gap failures**, unchanged from its pre-repair baseline.
resolved-by (full):
**Two scope facts recorded rather than left implicit. summary (full):
**`CloudService::nam()` SATISFIES THE LETTER OF THE AFFINITY RULING AND DEFEATS ITS POINT — it ACCOMMODATES an off-affinity first use instead of catching it.** Current bytes: `QNetworkAccessManager *created = new QNetworkAccessManager();` (constructed on the CALLER's thread), then `if (created->thread() != thread()) created->moveToThread(thread());`, then `created->setParent(this);`. The accepted ruling is that **creation must occur in the provider object's affinity thread**; creating it elsewhere and relocating it is not that. **The code argues against itself:** its own comment says the production threads already agree and that the check exists so the assumption is not "a silent one" — then implements silent accommodation rather than detection. User-identified 2026-08-27; orchestrator-verified in the working tree at `src/Cloud/CloudService.cpp:74-107`.
disposition (full):
**FIXED 2026-08-29 (CLOSED) — REPAIRED AND ORCHESTRATOR-VERIFIED IN THE ACCEPTED SLICE; BLOCKS: {} (was {TASK:DEC-040 Stage 1, CHECKPOINT:provider-watchdog slice}).** `CloudService.cpp` now GUARDS instead of accommodating: `nam()` refuses to initialize off-affinity (`if (QThread::currentThread() != thread())` with a diagnostic), constructs in-thread as `nam_ = new QNetworkAccessManager(this)` — the parentless-then-`moveToThread` dance is gone — and adoption of an injected manager is CONDITIONAL ON AFFINITY rather than a cross-thread `setParent()`. T-153(d) was rewritten accordingly and is green in the 155/155 run. Correction was dispatched to the builder mid-flight, before any further implementation or testing. Required shape: `nam()` may initialize ONLY while executing in the object's affinity thread; **assert/guard `QThread::currentThread() == thread()`**; construct and parent IN that thread (`new QNetworkAccessManager(this)` — the parentless-then-reparent dance disappears because the affinity is already correct); and **validate a constructor-INJECTED manager's affinity before adopting it** rather than moving it. **T-153(d) must be REWRITTEN**: the current shape (call `nam()` from the main thread, assert the manager moved elsewhere) is satisfiable ONLY by the behaviour being deleted, so it would have locked the defect in. Replacement: start the target `QThread` and invoke `nam()` on the service IN that thread via a queued/blocking-queued invocation, asserting affinity established by where it was CREATED.
resolved-by (full):
**THE ASSERT IS SAFE ON EVERY PRODUCTION PATH — orchestrator-verified rather than assumed, because this is the one place the correction could have forced a DEC-040 deviation.** Auto-download: `CloudServiceAutoDownload::run()` builds its instances INSIDE `run()` via `newService(worklist[i], context)` (`CloudService.cpp:3669`), so instance affinity IS the worker thread that then calls them. GUI sites (`Dropbox::createFolder`, `Azum`/`Nolio::listAthletes`) are constructed and used on the GUI thread. The one cross-thread call onto a MAIN-THREAD-constructed factory TEMPLATE from the worker — `service(name)->syncOnStartupSettingName()` at `:3650` — is a pure string builder (`CloudService.h:371`) and never reaches `nam()`. **No deviation is owed.**
