### ORCH-055 (line 497, Reviewer/DEC-040 Stage 2 piece 3b, T-148 (2026-09-05)) — full pre-compaction record, migrated by librarian Job-3 compaction 2026-09-06
summary (full):
**T-148's "GUI-thread default-token" ROWS DO NOT ACTUALLY TEST THE DEFAULT — THEY TEST A FRESH `CancelToken()` EXPLICITLY REASSIGNED OVER IT.** `fixture::driveSite(...)`'s 4th parameter, `CancelToken cancelToken = CancelToken()` (added piece 3a), is used by the callee UNCONDITIONALLY: the function body calls `service->setCancelToken(cancelToken)` regardless of whether the caller supplied an argument or fell through to the default (`testCloudProviderWatchdog.cpp` around lines 1115/1128). So `guiThread_defaultTokenNeverCancels()`'s three rows (piece 3b, T-148) never leave `CloudService::cancelToken_` untouched — they overwrite it with a freshly-constructed `CancelToken()`, which is behaviourally identical to the member's own in-class default ONLY if that default is itself correct. The row can therefore catch a broken `CancelToken::cancelled()` (which the piece-3b mutation proof, independently reproduced by the orchestrator, DID catch), but cannot catch a broken MEMBER INITIALIZATION — e.g. a constructor that mistakenly gave `cancelToken_` an always-cancelling starting value would be silently overwritten back to a working default by `driveSite` before the site method ever ran, and the test would stay green over a real production defect. Found by an independent reviewer reading the harness, not by execution.
disposition (full):
**FIXED 2026-09-05.** `fixture::driveSite`'s 4th parameter changed from `CancelToken cancelToken = CancelToken()` to `std::optional<CancelToken> cancelToken = std::nullopt`, and the body from an unconditional `service->setCancelToken(cancelToken);` to `if (cancelToken) service->setCancelToken(*cancelToken);` — "no token supplied" now genuinely skips the setter, so T-148's 3 rows rely entirely on `CloudService`'s own construction-time default for `cancelToken_`. The one explicit-token caller (`shapeBC_cancellationBreaksTheListing`) needed no change — `std::optional` converts implicitly from its value type. **Proven closed by mutation, not merely by inspection:** mutated `CloudService.h`'s own member default to start already-cancelled (`CancelToken cancelToken_ = CancelToken(std::make_shared<std::atomic_bool>(true));`, the exact defect class this row named) — RED on all 3 `guiThread_defaultTokenNeverCancels` rows under the FIXED harness (which the OLD unconditional-setCancelToken harness could not have caught, since it always overwrote `cancelToken_` with a fresh working token before the site method ran); the 11-test explicit-token isolation set stayed green under the identical mutation. Restored (`cmp` exit 0), full suite re-confirmed 168/0 both backends, full `ctest -L garmin-fast` **27/27 passed, EXIT=0, 230.42s**. Durable log: `.claude/evidence-seals/DEC040-Stage2-ORCH055-T148-harness-fix-2026-09-05.log`. **Original finding, preserved verbatim below:** OPEN, non-blocking — `{TASK:test-quality}`. Does not retroactively invalidate the piece-3b `CancelToken::cancelled()` mutation proof (that proof is real, for the property it actually tested), but T-148's OWN stated criterion — "GUI-thread caller bound with default (never-cancelling) token" — was not yet honestly covered. Owed: change `driveSite` (or add a sibling entry point) so "no token supplied" genuinely SKIPS the `setCancelToken` call rather than passing a default-constructed one — e.g. `std::optional<CancelToken>` with `std::nullopt` meaning "don't call the setter", or two overloads — so cancellation tests (piece 3a's `shapeBC_cancellationBreaksTheListing`, `table_row4`/`table_row6_cancelInduced...`) explicitly opt in and T-148's rows genuinely rely on `CloudService`'s own construction-time default. Then re-run the targeted T-148 rows plus the full suite on both QPA backends.
resolved-by (full):
Same shape as [[ORCH-053]] one row above: a test's claim to cover X is only as good as tracing what it ACTUALLY exercises, not what its name says — this is the third such gap surfaced in one session (rows 5/12/17's shape mislabels, ORCH-053's single-activity blind spot, now this). A pattern worth naming: this project's "add a token/cancel/flag through a shared helper's defaulted parameter" idiom needs the "did or didn't call the setter" distinction made STRUCTURALLY visible (a type, not a value), not inferred from what the value happens to be.

### ORCH-060 (line n/a — new row, librarian Job-3 compaction 2026-09-06) — historical compliance-gap finding
severity: informational
summary (full): STATE.md's own `## EVIDENCE`/`## LAST_CLV` history recorded 18 separate full

  2026-09-06), one per repair/build/reconciliation step. `references/orchestration.md`'s
  Scale-discipline section states: "The complete affected suite runs once per final content
  version, by one designated owner. A failed run followed by a repair, or any formatter/hook
  edit to a compiled or executed input, creates a new content version and requires a new run."
disposition (full): accept-with-note. Each of the 18 reruns corresponds to a genuinely NEW
  content version at the time it was run (a repair landed, a formatter/hook touched a compiled
  test file, or a checkpoint/gate closed) — so no single rerun, taken alone, was a duplicate of
  an unchanged content version, and the rule's letter was not violated on a per-run basis.
  The compliance gap is one of AGGREGATE DISCIPLINE, not a single violation: eighteen full-suite
  runs over one branch, several only stages/hours apart, is exactly the shape the Scale-discipline
  rule exists to bound, and no single session paused to ask "is a narrower targeted rerun +
  inspection sufficient here, reserving the full suite for the commit-ready handoff?" before
  reaching for the complete suite again. Acknowledged as a historical pattern, not reopened
  retroactively (the evidence it produced is not in question).
resolved-by (full): Going forward on this branch, the LEAN-EVIDENCE PROTOCOL applies: (1) during
  implementation, run the targeted test(s) for the mechanism under change plus ONE mutation proof
  per mechanism, not the complete suite; (2) run the complete `ctest -L garmin-fast` suite exactly
  ONCE per commit-ready handoff (i.e., immediately before the commit that will actually land),
  covering the FINAL content version of that handoff; (3) reserve BOTH Qt backends (`offscreen`
  AND `minimal`) for targets whose CHANGE touches async/lifecycle mechanisms (watchdogs, cancel
  tokens, teardown ordering) — an unrelated documentation-only or governance-only edit does not
  need a dual-backend rerun. No code or skill file is touched by this finding; it is a process
  record for this project's own history.

### ORCH-061 (line n/a — new row, librarian Job-3 compaction 2026-09-06) — proposed skill-level gap, NOT a compliance violation
severity: informational
summary (full): `unittests/Core/garminconnect/testCloudProviderWatchdog.cpp` and
  `testGarminConnectSyncDialogClose.cpp` have grown to roughly 8,874+ combined lines, 87+ test
  slots and a 512-seed fuzzer inside a SINGLE QTest binary/target. Splitting this target by
  mechanism (watchdog vs. dialog-close vs. fuzzer) was explicitly considered and NOT done,
  because QTest's function selector can INCLUDE named functions but cannot EXCLUDE one — a
  hand-split would require enumerating every OTHER slot by name in the "keep" half, and every
  slot added afterward would silently be dropped from whichever half the author forgot to touch.
  That is a worse defect (silent coverage loss) than the one a split would fix (one large binary).
disposition (full): deferred — this is NOT logged as a project compliance failure, because
  nothing in this project's currently-installed skill (`references/orchestration.md`,
  `references/lessons-memory.md`, or any qgdw-*.md agent prompt) states a fixture-growth cap or
  a split-by-mechanism rule for test binaries. There is no existing rule to have violated.
resolved-by (full): Recorded as a GENUINE SKILL-LEVEL GAP, proposed for the skill maintainer's
  own reference docs — NOT implemented here, per this project's standing convention that
  QGDW package fixes go upstream rather than patching the installed skill
  (`.claude/skills/quality-gated-dev-workflow/**` and the mirrored `.claude/agents/qgdw-*.md` are
  vendor territory, ORCH-004). Proposed rule shape for a future skill update: a fixture-growth cap
  (e.g. flag any single QTest binary once it exceeds a slot-count or line-count threshold) paired
  with a split-by-mechanism convention that only applies when the test framework in use supports
  an EXCLUDE selector (or an equivalent per-file target split at build-system level, not a
  hand-maintained function allowlist) — so a split cannot silently drop future slots the way a
  QTest include-only selector would. A companion lesson (LSN-085, `lessons.md`) records the
  lesson-miss recommending this be ported upstream into `lessons-memory.md`/`orchestration.md` by
  whoever maintains the skill package; this project does not and should not edit those files
  itself (see `qgdw-package-fixes-go-upstream` memory).

summary (full):
**REQ-NF-Obs-001's structured `gc_obs` trace lines are effectively invisible for live troubleshooting in the real qmake binary, and arrive out of order when they do arrive.** `gcObsTrace()` (`src/Cloud/GarminConnect.cpp:72-80`) emits one `gc_obs op=... outcome=... error_code=... duration_ms=...` line via `qDebug()` on every `open()` and every `readdir()` call, success and every early-return guard alike — the observability that DES-008/REQ-NF-Obs-001 exists to provide. `main.cpp`'s `nostderr()` (`src/Core/main.cpp:173-182`) redirects stderr with `freopen(file, "w", stderr)`. stderr's standard unbuffered property is NOT preserved across `freopen` onto a regular file: glibc gives the reopened stream full (block) buffering. GoldenCheetah's own `myMessageOutput` handler writes via `fprintf(stderr, ...)` and therefore accumulates in a ~4KB stdio buffer, while the embedded Python adapter writes to fd 2 DIRECTLY and lands immediately. Two consequences, both observed live tonight: (a) during a whole app session of Garmin troubleshooting the log showed only the Python-side `429` warnings and ZERO `gc_obs` lines, which actively misled diagnosis — the absence was read as 'the code path never executed' when in fact it had executed four times; (b) on clean exit the buffer flushed and all four lines appeared at once, INTERLEAVED OUT OF ORDER with the fd-2 writes (a startup Wayland-plugin line landed *after* the 429 pairs that chronologically followed it), so the log cannot be read as a timeline. Evidence: `~/.goldencheetah/goldencheetah.log` lines 18-22 after exit — `gc_obs op=auth outcome=fail error_code=unknown duration_ms=31/0/39/48` — none of which were present while the app ran. The trace code IS in the shipped binary (confirmed by a UTF-16 `strings -e l` scan finding the `QStringLiteral` format string; a default ASCII `strings` scan misses it and must not be used to conclude absence). Note the secondary signal in that evidence: all four carry `error_code=unknown`, i.e. the empty-token-blob restore of [[B-STAGE9-11]] folds to `GarminRestoreFailure::Unknown` rather than a distinct kind — the same undiagnosable-Unknown fold class as [[B-STAGE9-09]]

If it fails, the user must quit CLEANLY (File > Quit) so the buffered `gc_obs` lines flush — that is this very finding. — original assessment — **OPEN, blocking for REQ-NF-Obs-001's stated purpose.** Not a correctness defect in the Garmin feature itself — no user-visible behaviour changes — but it defeats the observability requirement precisely in the live-account scenario it was written for, and it demonstrably cost diagnostic time tonight. Candidate remedies, to be scored at dispatch (NOT yet decided): (a) `setvbuf(stderr, nullptr, _IOLBF, 0)` or `_IONBF` immediately after the `freopen` in `nostderr()` — smallest change, restores both liveness and ordering, but touches a shared non-Garmin file used by every GoldenCheetah subsystem; (b) an explicit `fflush(stderr)` at the end of `gcObsTrace()` only — Garmin-scoped, but fixes ordering only for our own lines and leaves every other `qDebug` caller buffered; (c) route `gc_obs` to a dedicated, separately-opened unbuffered stream/file — most isolated, but creates a second log the user must know about. summary (full):
`GarminTokenStore::loadChecked()` (`src/Cloud/GarminTokenStore.cpp:135-178`) reports a PRESENT, 0-byte token file at mode 0600 as `LoadStatus::Ok` with EMPTY `bytes`, so nothing downstream can distinguish an empty blob from a healthy one. Both guards pass it: the `!info.exists()` check at `:143` (the file does exist) and the REQ-006 owner-only permission check at `:157` (0600 is correct). The tail then unconditionally does `result.bytes = f.readAll(); result.status = LoadStatus::Ok;` with no content check at all. This violates the store's OWN documented contract: `src/Cloud/GarminTokenStore.h:33-47` defines `LoadStatus::Ok` as "file present, owner-only 0600, bytes returned" and `LoadResult::bytes` as "valid only when status == Ok". `GarminConnect::open()` (`src/Cloud/GarminConnect.cpp:470-491`) tests `r.isRejected()` then `!r.isOk()`; an empty-bytes `Ok` passes BOTH, so it proceeds to `blockingRestore(QString::fromUtf8(r.bytes), &restoreFailureKind)` at `:487` with an empty string, which fails and emits the REQ-005 generic copy "Garmin Connect: could not restore the stored session; please sign in again." with `gc_obs ... error_code=unknown` -- the same undiagnosable-Unknown fold class as [[B-STAGE9-09]], [[B-STAGE9-10]], [[B-STAGE9-11]] and [[B-STAGE9-12]], now a fifth time. Sequencing note, stated honestly: the PYTHON-side cause of the empty file was already fixed in `e5936375c` (`dump_tokens()` now calls `self._garmin.client.dumps()`), so a fresh connect should write a real blob. This is DEFENCE IN DEPTH on the C++ side -- it is not what makes sync work, and it must not be reported as such

Executed directly by the Inspector: `_validate_date_format('2026-09-09 05:21:24','startdate')` raises `ValueError: startdate must be in format YYYY-MM-DD, got: 2026-09-09 05:21:24`. Our side supplies exactly that rejected shape — `kGarminTimeFormat` (`src/Cloud/GarminConnect.cpp:54`) is the year-month-day hour-minute-second form, and ALL THREE sinceGmt sources (the dialog `from`, the backfill-state cursor, and the now-minus-7-days default) produce it — and `_list_activities_since_impl` (`src/Python/garminconnect/garmin_client.py:386`) forwards it VERBATIM. WHY IT FOLDS TO unknown: that call site catches only `GarminConnectConnectionError` and `GarminConnectTooManyRequestsError`, so a `ValueError` propagates unclassified; `with_retry`'s is_transient is False because it is not a `GarminError` at all, so there is no retry; and `classifyListException` (`src/Cloud/PyEmbeddedAdapter.cpp:485-497`) maps not-a-GarminError to `PyListOutcome::Unknown`. THE FOUR MEASURED LIVE SYMPTOMS ARE EXPLAINED BY THIS ONE CAUSE: it raises before any HTTP I/O (so 0-3ms is right), the library never logs it at a level we emit (so not one line appeared on fd 2 across every refresh), it is unclassified (so error_code=unknown), and it is deterministic on every call (so activity_count=0, fifteen times, zero downloads). THIS IS PRECISELY THE RISK DEC-014 OQ1 FLAGGED AND DEFERRED — the code comment at `garmin_client.py:378-384` says in its own words that the listing signature is unconfirmed against the not-yet-bundled wheel and that the surface is pinned by the fakes/pystub. The fakes accept a one-argument full-datetime call, so the suite stayed green while the real contract was broken; this is the fifth recorded instance of the verify-against-the-artifact-that-actually-runs class. WHAT IS OWED: a small Python-side unit — normalise sinceGmt to date-only before the library call (and decide explicitly whether the discarded time-of-day component needs same-day re-filtering on the results, since date-only listing widens the window to the whole start day), PLUS a fakes/pystub contract update so the stub rejects what the real wheel rejects. Without that second half the same class of defect stays invisible to the suite. NOT FIXED in [[B-STAGE9-19]]'s diff: `src/Python/garminconnect/garmin_client.py` was outside that builder's allowed paths and it correctly did not touch it. BLOCKS: {STAGE:9}
resolved-by (full):
Not yet resolved — repair GREEN in the working tree, UNREVIEWED, uncommitted. Filed by `garmin_inspector_v1_28` 2026-09-17 after independently re-executing the wheel's own validator and re-reading the forwarding call site, rather than accepting the builder's report. Any fix is owed an independent delta-check before it lands, per the standing rule that an Inspector's own read is not a substitute for one. **THREE REPAIR ROUNDS RAN 2026-09-18 and were never transcribed here at the time; reconstructed 2026-09-19 from the round artifacts before those were deleted, so this column is now the only record of them.** ROUND 1 (`garmin_codex_reviewer`, 3 BLOCKING + 1 non-blocking against the first fix): (a) a syntactically valid but semantically bad sidecar (`"lastSuccessStartTimeGMT":"not-a-date"`) reaches `date.fromisoformat(ts_gmt[:10])` and leaks a bare `ValueError` into the very unknown-fold this finding exists to abolish — `loadBackfillState` reads the value with `QJsonValue::toString()` and validates nothing; (b) swapping a full GMT lower bound for a date-only `startDate` widens the incremental window while `GarminConnect::readdir()` has no post-query `startTimeGMT > cursor` filter (only imported-ID removal), so with a torn imported-ID sidecar an older same-day activity is exposed and `recordImport()` writes it back as the cursor — the cursor moves BACKWARDS; (c) the wheel documents no timezone parameter and sorts `startLocal`, so UTC-day equivalence of `startDate` is unestablished — a west-of-UTC account can silently miss an activity that is after the cursor but outside the query; (d) non-blocking — `_validate_startdate_like_real_library()` did not mirror the real validator (regex only, so it accepted `2026-02-30`, which the real `strptime` path rejects). ROUND 2 repaired (a) as a typed `GarminError(kind='cursor_invalid')`, (b) as a post-query lower-bound filter plus a one-day-early query margin, and (d) by giving the fake strip/full-match/calendar parity; the reviewer then found 2 NEW BLOCKING defects IN that filter: (e) it compared raw STRING renderings, so `'2026-09-09T07:00:00' > '2026-09-09 18:00:00'` is True (`'T'` 0x54 > `' '` 0x20) and `str(None)` also sorts past a real date — an 11-hour-older record, or a null one, passes the filter and regresses the cursor, while an ISO-form cursor conversely drops valid space-form activities; (f) strict `>` permanently strands a legitimate second activity sharing a `startTimeGMT` second, since the resume cursor carries no activity-ID tie-breaker. ROUND 3 (`garmin_builder_stage9_v13`) repaired both: one module-level `_as_utc_instant()` used by BOTH the cursor and every response value so no second parser can drift, comparison over UTC instants rather than strings, `>=` with the residual stated rather than papered over, and a DISTINCT `response_invalid` kind kept separate from `cursor_invalid` on the argument that conflating them makes a server-side shape change masquerade as local state corruption. Builder evidence, SELF-REPORTED and not yet re-run by an Inspector: `test_adapter_list.py` 13 passed, `test_adapter_real_library_contract.py` 9 passed, `pytest tests/` 74 passed; 4 scripted mutations (M1 `>=`→`>`, M2 instants→strings, M3 non-string guard off, M4 `.get()`→`[]`) each went RED at the predicted point with byte-identical restores; ruff 0.6.9 and `mypy --strict` 1.11.2 clean; `ctest -R` over the two targets `testGarminConnectPyAdapter` and `testGarminConnectSync` 2/2. A deliberate behaviour change it flagged itself: the cursor parse got STRICTER — round 2's `[:10]` slice silently accepted `"2026-09-09 junk"`, the unified path raises `cursor_invalid` on it. WHAT IS OWED, and why this row is still open: (1) **the round-3 repair has never been independently reviewed** — the round-3 brief was delivered to `garmin_codex_reviewer` and that pane sat blocked on "Complete round 3 review" without ever returning a verdict, so the fixes for (e) and (f) rest solely on the builder's own report, which the standing rule above does not accept; (2) round 1's finding (c), the `startDate` timezone semantics, was never explicitly answered in round 2 or 3 — the one-day-early margin plus exact UTC-instant filtering plausibly subsumes it by construction, but nobody verified and closed it, so it must NOT be assumed discharged; (3) the work is GREEN but UNSTAGED and UNCOMMITTED in a tree carrying several unrelated in-flight workstreams, so it is one `git add -A` away from being mixed or lost; (4) the C++ `classifyListException` wiring gap (`PyEmbeddedAdapter.cpp:485-497`) that makes both typed kinds still fold to `Unknown` remains separately filed and outside the builder's allowed paths — today both kinds reach an operator only through the [[B-STAGE9-19]] `rawMessage` channel **ROUND 4 CLOSED IT (2026-09-19, `garmin_inspector_v1_30`).** The round-3 repair finally got the independent delta-check it was owed: `garmin_codex_reviewer` returned NO BLOCKING defect and closed (a)-(f). (c) was additionally put to an isolated investigator (`s925_tz_investigator`) against the installed wheel, which established that the listing sends only `startDate`/`start`/`limit` and NO timezone parameter (`garminconnect/__init__.py:2700-2714`) — so whether Garmin resolves `startDate` as UTC day or account-local day is NOT establishable from source and was NOT measured (no live account). RULING: (c) closes on a conditional-coverage argument valid under BOTH interpretations — a UTC-12 local midnight still falls >=12h before the cursor's UTC day begins, so a one-day-early query cannot exclude an instant newer than the cursor — with the unmeasured server behaviour recorded as an accepted residual, not as proof. The reviewer's own wording for (c) was more certain than the evidence supports and was deliberately not carried into this row. Inspector re-verification, not relayed: pytest 74/74; `mypy --strict` 1.11.2 clean on 16 files; mutations M1 (`>=`->`>`) and M2 (instants->strings) each RED in exactly the predicted slots, md5 byte-identical restore; ctest over `testGarminConnectPyAdapter` + `testGarminConnectSync` 4/4. ONE BUILDER SELF-REPORT WAS FALSE: it claimed ruff 0.6.9 clean, but the gate-pinned ruff 0.6.9 would have reformatted `test_adapter_list.py` (two asserts) — a newer ruff formats asserts differently. Repaired with the pinned binary; 16/16 formatted, suite still 74/74. Residual split out as its own row: [[B-STAGE9-26]].

### ORCH-063 (was findings.md line 507)
```text
| ORCH-063 | Inspector/B-STAGE9-16 Part B repair round 1 builder supervision (2026-09-16), `garmin_inspector_v1_26`. Hit within four minutes of the Inspector succession, while the builder was repairing R1-F1 — the wake caught the pane as `blocked` and the dialog was read, classified, and approved rather than routed around, per [[LSN-036]]'s own rule | non-blocking — tooling/process false-positive, not a code defect | Guard misses that `mkdir -p` made the dir its `cd` enters | OPEN, non-blocking, {TASK:hook-tooling}. A FIFTH distinct root cause under [[LSN-036]]'s standing class, and the first that is NOT a regex/parsing bug — it is a missing state update in the guard's own sequential walk. `_resolve_cd()` (`.claude/hooks/anti_duplication_guard.py:293-329`) ends with `return ap if os.path.isdir(ap) else None`, evaluated at HOOK time, i.e. BEFORE the command runs. So for the extremely ordinary scratch-probe shape `mkdir -p /tmp/probe && cd /tmp/probe && git init -q . && ...`, the `cd` target does not exist yet, `_resolve_cd` correctly returns None by its own documented contract, the effective cwd for the following relative operand (`.`) becomes unknown, and the run stops on the `unresolved_ask` message at `:609-618`. The guard's `shell_targets()` walk ALREADY parsed that same `mkdir -p` as a `mkdir_p` target moments earlier — the information needed to resolve the `cd` was in hand and simply never fed back into the existence model. Note the failure is an ASK, not a DENY (`:607` states the never-deny-a-guessed-path policy deliberately), so it is milder than [[ORCH-058]]'s denial — but under LSN-036 an ASK on a legitimate read-only operation still costs a human keypress and still trains bypass, which is the damage the lesson is actually about. Not fixed here, and deliberately NOT patched locally: the standing rule is that quality-gated-dev-workflow package bugs ship UPSTREAM, because a local patch is a fork the next reinstall silently reverts — proven both ways on 2026-08-05. Suggested upstream fix, stated so it is reviewable rather than hand-waved: while walking the command left to right, treat a successfully-parsed `mkdir`/`mkdir -p` of an ABSOLUTE path as making that directory exist for the remainder of the same command's resolution, so a subsequent `cd` into it resolves. That is strictly narrower than relaxing `_resolve_cd`, and it cannot introduce a clobber blind spot, because the `mkdir` target itself is still classified by the existing rules | Sibling in kind to [[ORCH-058]] and [[ORCH-062]] — same hook, third and now fourth distinct detection path (snapshot-restore suffix regex; new-file-creation regex; and now `cd`-resolution existence checking). Workaround in use meanwhile, and it is a workaround for the AGENT, not for the guard: write scratch scripts with the Write tool and invoke them by absolute path, or run the `mkdir` as its own separate step, rather than chaining. [[LSN-036]] miss recorded (miss:5) in the same edit as this row. No REQ allocated; flagged for whoever next owns hook maintenance upstream. |
```

### ORCH-064 (was findings.md line 508)
```text
| ORCH-064 | Found by `garmin_inspector_v1_30` 2026-09-19 after the USER asked why no wake had fired even though the reviewer had finished 14 minutes earlier — the Inspector had reported the wake "armed successfully" on the absence of an immediate error rather than on evidence it could fire | non-blocking — Inspector tooling, no product code affected | insp_wake.sh never fired on its success path | **FIXED 2026-09-19.** `exec > >(tee -a $WAKELOG)` makes `tee` a child of the script; the bare `wait` after `kill $(jobs -p)` waits for every child including `tee`, which cannot exit while the script still holds the pipe open. Deadlock. Reproduced standalone (exit 124, the block never printed) and re-verified after the fix (exit 0; the real script now prints the block and exits). Fix: wait on the `herdr agent wait` children BY PID, never via bare `wait`/`jobs -p`. Why it stayed invisible: the roster-error path `exit 1`s before reaching any `wait`, so the only arm that had ever produced output was a failure, and the success path had never once completed. ### ORCH-067 (was findings.md line 511)
```
```text
| ORCH-067 | Raised by the USER 2026-09-19, twice: first "why you did not receive any wake so far", then "why did you decide to stop?" Both times the Inspector (`garmin_inspector_v1_30`) had reported the loop healthy. Filed because the second question exposed a defect the first one's fix did not touch | non-blocking — process/skill defect, no product code affected | Arming a wake with nothing dispatched is a no-op that reads as supervision | **open.** The Inspector closed an atomic unit, named the next one (B-STAGE9-12), did NOT dispatch it, armed `insp_wake.sh` and ended the turn. With all three agents idle the wake takes its settled branch and waits `--until working` — a transition only a dispatch from the Inspector can cause — so the loop could not self-advance and the next wake was a pure poll. The `SKILL.md` invariant that was satisfied is the MECHANICAL one ("never end a turn without a wake armed"); the actual requirement (keep going) is checked by nothing, so arming the wake functioned as a substitute for working. Two aggravating factors, both the Inspector's: it cited its own context at 176k against a 210k threshold as if succession were imminent, and it treated a landed commit as a finish line. PARTIAL FIX APPLIED 2026-09-19 (uncommitted at time of writing): the settled heartbeat cut 900000 -> 300000 so a stall surfaces in 5 minutes rather than 15, the header now warns that passing both positional args overrides the defaults (editing the default alone silently does nothing), and `SKILL.md` gained an explicit clause that all-idle-with-nothing-dispatched is always an Inspector error, not a wait. WHAT IS OWED: the heartbeat change treats VISIBILITY only — no timeout length can release a branch that waits on a dispatch nobody made. A mechanical guard belongs in the wake itself: refuse to arm, or print a loud stall warning, when every roster pane is settled and no work is outstanding. BLOCKS: {} | — |
```

Practical effect on the user right now: Garmin Connect is configured and working, but the session is not restorable, so credentials must be re-entered after an app restart. Deliberately excluded from B-STAGE9-09's atomic unit (builder correctly flagged rather than fixed, staying inside its assigned scope). It cannot fail the connect itself: `PyEmbeddedAdapter.cpp:618-633` sets `out.kind = PyAuthOutcome::Success` BEFORE calling `dump_tokens`, then on any failure clears the pending error and leaves `tokenBlob` empty, under an explicit contract comment ("A dump failure must NOT fail an otherwise-successful auth ... the worker treats empty as 'nothing to persist'"). That deliberate degrade-don't-fail design, made for REQ-004, is what keeps this defect off the critical path for attempt #5 — the user will connect successfully but will have to re-enter credentials after a restart until this is fixed. Queue order for `garmin_builder_stage9_v3` after B-STAGE9-09 lands: this and [[B-STAGE9-10]] together are the remaining DEC-014 OQ1 residuals and should be dispatched as ONE unit with a shared real-wheel signature/contract test extending `test_adapter_real_library_contract.py` (the guard B-STAGE9-09 introduced), since both are the same root cause and both need the same class of executable check — an existence check is insufficient for the MFA half, whose defect is argument ORDER.
